articles.title: Lionel Messi Scores 100th Inter Miami Goal In Campeones Cup Final Win vs. Cruz Azul
articles.summary: Lionel Messi scored the 100th goal of his Inter Miami career and Casemiro added another as Miami defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup.
articles.body: Lionel Messi scored the 100th goal of his Inter Miami career and Casemiro added another as Miami defeated Cruz Azul 2-0 on Wednesday night to win the Campeones Cup. Messi opened the scoring in the 24th minute, heading in a cross from Luis Suárez for his 100th goal in 115 appearances across all competitions with Miami. The milestone came against the same club Messi scored his first Inter Miami goal against. He scored on a stoppage-time free kick to beat Cruz Azul 2-1 in his Miami debut in July 2023. Casemiro made it 2-0 in the 81st minute, heading in a corner from Messi. The Brazilian midfielder has scored four goals, all headers, in his last five matches after scoring in three consecutive games against CF Montreal, Atlanta United and Chicago before being held scoreless Saturday against Nashville. The victory gave Inter Miami another trophy three years after Messi’s arrival. Miami won the Leagues Cup in 2023, the Supporters’ Shield in 2024 and MLS Cup in 2025. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Tom Brady Has Seen Enough: Patrick Mahomes Is Back To Being Himself
articles.summary: Tom Brady is not ready to dismiss the Kansas City Chiefs disappear from the Super Bowl contender conversation.
articles.body: Tom Brady is not ready to dismiss the Kansas City Chiefs from the Super Bowl contender conversation. In fact, he's making a big declaration about the Chiefs and quarterback Patrick Mahomes. In his latest NFL power rankings, Brady placed the Chiefs at No. 7 and he thinks Mahomes is playing like himself again after tearing his ACL last December. "I think, in a lot of ways, he's back to [being] Patrick Mahomes," Brady said. "What do I mean by that? His leadership, discipline, tenacity — all of those things were on display. He's going to pick up some steam. He's missed some football, missed a lot of the offseason. But never sleep on No. 15 for the Chiefs." Mahomes didn't have the strongest stat line in the Chiefs' 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos on Monday night. He completed 15 of 27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns and an interception. But he also ran for a 15-yard score in the first quarter, making a vintage Mahomes-like play. "Patrick Mahomes, are you kidding me? He might be able to contribute something to this offense as well," Brady said. He wasn't avoiding any contact [on Monday night]; I'm sure of that. Statistically, Mahomes wasn't the catalyst of the Chiefs' offense on Monday night. Newcomer Kenneth Walker III dominated on the ground. He rushed for a career-high 173 yards on 7.5 yards per carry and a touchdown, with that 60-yard score giving Kansas City a decisive advantage in the second half. Walker's performance earned a shout-out from Brady. However, the bulk of Brady's commentary focused on Mahomes, giving him an endorsement as many have compared the two quarterbacks' careers. Brady also returned from an ACL injury around the same time as Mahomes did in his career, so he knows what the Chiefs star is going through. And as the Chiefs have the three-time Super Bowl winner back at quarterback, he made it clear he isn't buying the idea that Kansas City is fading. "Why are we counting them out? Never count them out," Brady said. Brady closed with the same logic that's carried the Chiefs through multiple championship runs already: put the right coach with the right quarterback in an organization built on winning, and the results tend to follow. "I always felt like when you've got a great coach and you've got a great QB, and that organization has championship standards … watch out, man. articles.title: La atleta que compitió cubierta en heces pide disculpas y renuncia a su triunfo en el Hyrox de Pekín
articles.standfirst: Joanna Wietrzyk sufrió una incontinencia estomacal durante la prueba pero siguió hasta el final y otros participantes se mancharon o incluso resbalaron por culpa de sus necesidades
articles.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk sufrió una incontinencia estomacal durante la prueba pero siguió hasta el final y otros participantes se mancharon o incluso resbalaron por culpa de sus necesidades
articles.body: El caso de Joanna Wietrzyk, actual campeona del mundo de Hyrox, ha dado la vuelta al mundo. La australiana se hizo viral tras sufrir una incontinencia estomacal mientras competía en Pekín. Wietrzyk se hizo sus necesidades encima, pero siguió compitiendo y acabó llevándose la victoria cubierta en heces. Un final con polémica tras la queja de varios participantes en la prueba. "La limpieza no se realizó en ese momento, sino al final del día, y hubo personas que se mancharon e incluso resbalaron por las heces", señaló hace unos días una participante a EFE. La indignación fue creciendo con el paso de las horas hacia los organizadores, ya que en esta competición se penaliza escupir en la pista o verterse agua por encima, pero no se penalizó a la australiana y se le dejó seguir compitiendo. Tras las quejas, Hyrox se vio obligado a cambiar las reglas. Este jueves ha sido la propia deportista la que ha usado su perfil de Instagram para pedir disculpas por no haberse retirado de la competición. "Quiero ofrecer mis sinceras disculpas a la gente de China, mis compañeros competidores, los espectadores y los organizadores de HYROX por lo que sucedió durante la carrera en Pekín", comienza. La australiana explica que nada hacía presagiar antes del evento lo que luego sucedería. "Me sentí completamente en forma y saludable al comienzo de la carrera, sin ninguna razón para esperar ninguna enfermedad. Mirando hacia atrás, lamento la decisión de no haberme salido de la pista. Reconozco que debería haber hecho una elección diferente. Asumo la responsabilidad por mi decisión de continuar y lamento profundamente las molestias y las interrupciones que causó", añade. Y anuncia que renuncia a la victoria: "Sé que mis acciones tuvieron un impacto más allá de mí misma, y realmente lo siento por todos los que se vieron afectados. Estoy aprendiendo de esta experiencia y llevaré esas lecciones conmigo, incluyendo recordar que hay más en la vida que correr y saber cuándo es correcto alejarse. Reflexionando, he decidido retirarme retroactivamente de la carrera y perder los puntos que gané". Termina su comunicado agradeciendo a quienes le han apoyado. "Me tomaré un tiempo para recuperarme, reflexionar y cuidar de mí y de mi familia lejos del ruido", dijo

articles.title: Deion Sanders is "ten toes down" after receiving new prosthetic toes
articles.summary: Deion Sanders revealed custom prosthetic toes designed to improve his balance, alignment and comfort after his 2021 amputations.
articles.body:
Colorado football coach Deion Sanders is once again "ten toes down" after receiving new prosthetic toes for his left foot, following the amputation of two toes in 2021 due to life-threatening blood clots.

Sanders took to social media to show off his custom silicone prosthetics, designed to replace his left foot's largest toes. These new additions will help support his foot, improve balance, and restore proper alignment, allowing him to bear weight more comfortably.

"This is amazing," Sanders said in his social media video. "It feels like it's dragging, but guess what? I am ten toes down again."

Sanders first spoke publicly about his amputation in March 2022, capturing the journey in his "Coach Prime" documentary series . The show included footage of Sanders in a hospital bed, looking at his foot for the first time and coming to terms with the aftermath of his surgery.

He explained that the amputation became necessary after he developed severe blood clots following a September 2021 procedure to repair a dislocated toe and inflamed nerve. As his condition worsened, doctors discussed the possibility of amputating his left leg from the knee down.

Fortunately, after multiple surgeries, only his left big toe and second toe had to be removed.

articles.title: Bus mix-ups, leaking cabins and hotel shortages: With 17,000 athletes arriving, Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya face logistical problems and typhoon fears
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Nagoya was flattened during World War II, it was a primary target for US strategic bombing during World War II because it served as Japan’s major hub .
articles.body: Nagoya was flattened during World War II, it was a primary target for US strategic bombing during World War II because it served as Japan’s major hub for aircraft and munitions manufacturing. During World War II, Nagoya suffered extensive damage from air raids due to its role as an industrial center. The city’s industrial facilities, including the castle, were largely destroyed. However, the post-war period would see Nagoya rise from these ashes to become one of Japan’s most important industrial and economic centers.More than eight decades later, the Japanese city is hosting thousands of athletes and officials for the Asian Games, but the build-up to the event has been marked by problems with accommodation and transport.Defending Asian Games men's football champions South Korea were late for a training session on Wednesday after the bus arranged for the team failed to arrive at their hotel, Reuters reported.The Koreans, who opened their campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Games with a 4-1 win over Qatar on Tuesday, reached their recovery session in Nagoya 20 minutes late after officials had to arrange a replacement bus.The transport problem came a day after another mix-up involving the South Korean team. The bus taking them to their opening match went to a baseball ground instead of the Mizuho Rugby Stadium. The team eventually reached the stadium 30 minutes after the scheduled arrival time.The incidents have added to a series of concerns around transport and accommodation ahead of the official opening of the Asian Games in Japan on Saturday. Some events, including football, have already begun before the opening ceremony.The 20th Asian Games will bring together more than 17,000 athletes and officials, including Olympic and world champions. The Games are being held mainly in the port city of Nagoya and across the wider Aichi prefecture, with competition running until October 4.Nagoya has more than two million residents and is the fourth biggest city in Japan by population.The Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, which can hold 30,000 people, will be the main venue for the Games and will host athletics as well as the opening and closing ceremonies. Swimming, one of the most closely watched events, will be held 350 kilometres (200 miles) east in Tokyo.The Games are being held every four years, with places at the 2028 Olympics also up for grabs in some events.More than 17,000 competitors and officialsAccommodation has been one of the main issues in the build-up to the Games. South Korea's Olympic committee said on Monday there was "a serious shortage of accommodation" at the event, while officials from the Philippines turned to Airbnb.The problem continued into Thursday, with even the host Japan team looking at alternative arrangements after cases in which male and female athletes were allocated shared rooms.Local organisers had initially expected about 15,000 athletes and officials to attend. They later said they had "neither the manpower nor the budget" to deal with the higher number.Organisers subsequently issued a joint statement with the Olympic Council of Asia saying that all athletes and officials registered before the July deadline would be "provided with Games-appropriate accommodation".More than 17,000 competitors and officials are expected to attend the Games.Accommodation and transport problemsThe number of participants, which is higher than at the Olympics, has created problems for organisers who initially planned for 15,000 people and have had to find accommodation for the additional participants.They decided not to build a dedicated athletes' village in order to reduce costs. Instead, athletes and officials are being housed in a mix of hotels, a cruise ship and temporary accommodation, including wooden cabins and shipping container-style huts.Organisers have said the 20th edition of the Games, first held in 1951, will be "the most spectacular for generations".Between 4,000 and 5,000 athletes and officials will stay on the Italian cruise ship Costa Serena. The ship has 571 cabins, seven swimming pools, eight restaurants and nine bars.Cruise ships have previously been used as accommodation at international sporting events, but never on this scale.The arrangement has raised concerns among some participating countries. India even built replica container huts to prepare its athletes for their stay in Japan.A senior coach accompanying India's 30-member shooting contingent has also expressed disappointment with the arrangements, particularly the amount of time needed to travel between the accommodation and the training and competition venue.The coach, as quoted by PTI, said he had arrived in Japan with a certain level of expectation but felt the arrangements had not matched the image he had of the country. Indian shooters have been housed around 50km from the range and in different hotels.For a contingent that includes several of India's medal hopefuls, including double Olympic bronze medallist Manu Bhaker and multiple Asian Games medallist Esha Singh, the commute has meant early starts and long hours on the road to maintain their training schedules.“This (transportation) is a real problem. But what can we do about it? I didn’t see any hotels in the vicinity of the shooting range. If there were, we would have reached early. They gave us accommodation at a place which was far, so now what can we do about it?” the coach, who was not named, said, as quoted by PTI.South Korean sports officials on Monday described the accommodation facilities as "the worst" they had experienced at the Games and said the beds were too short.With only days remaining before the opening ceremony, a Korean Olympic committee official was quoted as saying by AFP that there was "a serious shortage of accommodation".There have also been concerns about the condition of the shipping container-style huts, which are expected to house around 2,000 athletes and officials.South Korean basketball player Byeon Jun-hyeong posted a video on social media showing a leaking sink and a wet floor inside his hut.He posted the caption, "Please help us".Typhoon adds to concernsJapan did not build a dedicated athletes' village as part of its effort to reduce costs. Some competitors are staying in hotels, while others are being housed on a cruise liner docked at Nagoya's port. Temporary wooden cabins are also being used.Organisers have said the cruise ship will provide a memorable experience for those staying on board, but weather conditions could create another problem.September and October are typhoon season in Japan. The Costa Serena can house about 4,000 people and is the twin ship of the Costa Concordia, which sank off Tuscany in 2012, killing 32 people.The weather has already caused problems for the Games. Last week, heavy rainfall hit Nagoya and forced participants staying in the shipping container-style accommodation to evacuate temporarily.Several teams have complained about the condition of the huts, including the length of the beds, while others have raised concerns about a shortage of rooms.On Thursday, two days before the opening ceremony, weather forecasters predicted that a typhoon could hit Japan's main island, where Nagoya is located, on Sunday or Monday.Such weather could affect the estimated 4,000 Games participants staying on the cruise ship in Nagoya's port."All we can do is to pray that the worst-case scenario will not happen," The Asahi Shimbun quoted an unnamed sports federation official as saying.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck's Trade Request Addressed by Jets GM amid Goalie's Camp Absence
articles.summary: Winnipeg Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff says he is willing to wait in order to find the right trade for Connor Hellebuyck despite the star netminder's refusal to report to training camp.
articles.body:
Winnipeg Jets general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff says he is willing to wait in order to find the right trade for Connor Hellebuyck despite the star netminder's refusal to report to training camp.

"This isn't necessarily a time thing for me. My obligation is to the Winnipeg Jets players and the Winnipeg Jets fans, and for me, I just want to get this right," Cheveldayoff told reporters Thursday.

Asked whether there was any prior understanding Hellebuyck would seek a trade if the Jets weren't competitive in the future, Cheveldayoff answered, "A contract is a contract in the National Hockey League, period. There are no side agreements."

The Jets have been navigating Hellebuyck's trade request since exit meetings following the regular-season finale in April, according to Cheveldayoff.

"When Connor came and asked, and requested being traded, we kept it quiet. That was partly on his request as well," Cheveldayoff said. "We tried to make that work, and we've been trying to make it work ever since."

The general manager's media availability took place the day after Hellebuyck did not report to Wednesday training camp and was subsequently suspended by the team.

Hellebuyck said in an Aug. 27 statement shared by his agent, Ray Petkau, that he had requested a trade "several months ago."

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck wrote at the end of August.

Cheveldayoff said Hellebuyck's camp had warned the team in earlier conversations they might release a statement if the goaltender's trade request was not resolved, but indicated the Jets would still be willing to welcome Hellebuyck back should he decide to rejoin the team.

"No doors are closed, in my estimation. He's a player under contract, and he's a player that's under contract for five years," Cheveldayoff said. "At the end of the day, that's his choice."

Cheveldayoff concluded, "It can't get emotional. It can't get personal. Connor Hellebuyck is part of our family until he's not part of our family."

Hellebuyck has played the entirety of his NHL career with the Jets since the team drafted him in 2012. He is under contract through the 2030-31 season on the seven-year, $8.5 million extension he signed in October 2023.

Although Hellebuyck won back-to-back Vezina Trophies over his next two seasons since signing that contract, the Jets didn't get any closer to the franchise's first Stanley Cup.

The team suffered two early-round eliminations before missing out on the postseason altogether last spring.

Hellebuyck has a full no-move clause on his contract through the 2026-27 season, per PuckPedia .

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman previously reported Hellebuyck's list of teams he would be willing to accept a trade to is "much wider than some of the other players who've asked for trades," which could be a nod to Dylan Larkin's reported three-team list of Stanley Cup contenders.

Friedman noted, however, he expects it is unlikely Hellebuyck would approve a trade to another Canadian team.

Cheveldayoff said Thursday that discussing potential trades with teams on Hellebuyck's list has been complicated both by the return the Jets are seeking for a three-time Vezina Trophy winner and the relatively limited market for starting goaltenders.

"We're talking about moving Connor Hellebuyck... We expect that a level of return would be commensurate to that," Cheveldayoff said. "There has been nothing that has allowed us to say 'Okay, this works for both parties.'"

Cheveldayoff continued, sayig, "We're talking about a goaltender here, which is different than talking about a center, different than talking about a defenseman. If you're a team that has a bona fide No. 1 goaltender, and he's locked up, and he's yours, you're probably not interested.

"A team might be on the list as an available option, has a No. 1 goaltender, that's a moot point."

For now, the Jets will head into the season with Stuart Skinner, who split last season between the Edmonton Oilers and Pittsburgh Penguins, as their top option.

Barring a change in Hellebuyck's situation or a trade, Skinner and Thomas Milic of the AHL's Manitoba Moose could be the Jets' tandem when the puck drops on Oct. 2 for the season opener in Winnipeg.

articles.title: Hyrox Athlete 'Genuinely Sorry' After Soiling Herself During Competition in Beijing
articles.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk, a Hyrox athlete who competed in an indoor fitness event last weekend, has issued an apology for remaining on the track after soiling herself during the competition.
articles.body:
Joanna Wietrzyk, a Hyrox athlete who competed in an indoor fitness event last weekend, has issued an apology for remaining on the track after soiling herself during the competition.

In a statement posted to her Instagram page, Wietrzyk wrote she is "genuinely sorry" to everyone who was affected by the situation and is retroactively withdrawing from the race:

"Personal statement: I want to offer my sincere apology to the people of China, my fellow competitors, the spectators and the HYROX organizers for what happened during the race in Beijing.

"I felt completely fit and healthy at the start of the race, with no reason to expect any illness. Looking back, I regret the decision to not have stepped off the track. I recognize that I should have made a different choice. I take responsibility for my decision to continue and am deeply sorry for the discomfort and disruption it caused.

"I know my actions had an impact beyond myself, and I am genuinely sorry to everyone who was affected. I am learning from this experience and will carry those lessons with me, including remembering that there is more to life than racing and knowing when it is right to step away. On reflection, I have decided to retroactively withdraw from the race and forfeit the points I earned."

Hyrox is a fitness competition that combines running and functional exercises. Participants will run one kilometer, then do one functional workout and repeat the pattern eight times.

Some of the functional workouts include sled pushes and pulls, burpees, rowing and lunges while carrying sandbags. Athletes typically use shared equipment during competitions.

Wietrzyk took part in a Hyrox event in Beijing on Saturday. Around the midway point, she soiled herself but continued with the competition and went on to win.

Hyrox co-founder Moritz Fürste issued an apology on Sunday, writing it was a "mistake" not reacting immediately, and new rules and procedures have been put in place to prevent this type of situation from happening in the future.

Hyrox was originally founded in 2017 by Fürste, a three-time Olympic medalist in field hockey, and Christian Toetzke. Its first event was held in Germany in 2018.

articles.title: Alex Ovechkin Updates Retirement Timeline Ahead of 2026-27 NHL Season with Capitals
articles.summary: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin isn't closing the door on the possibility of extending the NHL's all-time goalscoring record beyond the upcoming season.
articles.body:
Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin isn't closing the door on the possibility of extending the NHL's all-time goalscoring record beyond the upcoming season.

Ovechkin told reporters Thursday he hasn't yet decided whether he will return for another season after the 2026-27 campaign, per Capitals reporter Sammi Silber.

"I have to make the team," Ovechkin joked, per Silber.

Ovechkin, 41, is set to be one of the oldest active players in the NHL after re-signing with the Capitals on a one-year deal this offseason.

He joins Colorado Avalanche defenseman Brent Burns and Los Angeles Kings winger Corey Perry as the NHL's only active players over 40.

Ovechkin told reporters Thursday he made the decision to return for another season after watching the Capitals' moves at the trade deadline and in free agency (h/t Capitals radio broadcaster John Walton).

The Capitals' moves since the spring have included acquiring defenseman Timothy Liljegren and extending top-line winger Ryan Leonard.

"The new faces, what we have, it will give us a chance to fight for a Cup," Ovechkin said.

Ovechkin declined throughout the 2025-26 season to confirm if he would be returning for another NHL campaign. He closed out the Capitals' final home game of the season by declining a handshake line arranged by the Pittsburgh Penguins.

He finally announced his intention to return for another season in July, at which point Ovechkin did not shut down the possibility of also playing in the 2027-28 campaign.

Ovechkin, who broke Wayne Gretzky's all-time goalscoring record in April 2025, scored 32 goals and played all 82 games for the Capitals last season.

Outside of the pandemic-shortened campaign in 2020-21, Ovechkin has scored more than 30 goals in 20 consecutive NHL campaigns.

He led the league in goalscoring seven times in eight years between 2012 and 2020, including a 2017-18 campaign he capped off by leading the Caps to the franchise's first Stanley Cup.

The Capitals will now hope to celebrate the return of NHL's leading goalscorer by making it back to the playoffs after missing out last season. That push will start Oct. 2 with a regular-season opener on the road against the defending champion Carolina Hurricanes.

articles.body: Indian MMA athlete Varun Sanyal has spoken about the problems he faced after arriving in Japan for the Asian Games, where the sport is making its debut at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Sanyal, a bronze medallist at the Asian Championships in China in January 2026, travelled from London to Nagoya via Mumbai and Singapore. He had an official accreditation ID card, which also serves as his visa, but said officials were still unable to locate his details.He said he was left waiting for around three hours without a clear resolution or food before being moved between different venues and eventually directed to the Costa Serena cruise ship, which is being used to house athletes."It's been one crazy day, and it's still not over. I thought it was done, but it's not. There's a lot of chaos with regards to the athletes' rooms and assignment of rooms. Had this happened in India, 100% this would be a bigger deal. The media would be running wild with it, and India as a country wouldn't hear the end of it," Sanyal said in the now-deleted video.Sanyal said the problems began soon after he arrived in Nagoya.“When you get to Nagoya, from the airport they take you on a shuttle... and as soon as you get there, it's total chaos. I go to the counter... and they just cannot find my name anywhere in the system. Like, I'm a total ghost in their system. This took about two hours... I'm not exaggerating, two hours they're like running around. By the time we left that facility, it had been three hours. By the way, my situation wasn't solved,” he added.The delay also meant that Sanyal was unable to get food during the wait."In none of these facilities was there any food. They'd give you water bottles, but there's no food and you can't even go anywhere and buy anything," he said."Yes, I know as an MMA fighter or perhaps a wrestler, boxer, you're cutting weight, etc., but you still need to eat. You still need some kind of food."At the third facility, Sanyal said he met athletes from Tajikistan and Sri Lanka who were facing similar problems."Everyone is facing a similar issue. They later said they had "neither the manpower nor the budget" to deal with the higher number.Organisers subsequently issued a joint statement with the Olympic Council of Asia saying that all athletes and officials registered before the July deadline would be "provided with Games-appropriate accommodation".More than 17,000 competitors and officials are expected to attend the Games.The number of participants, which is higher than at the Olympics, has created problems for organisers who initially planned for 15,000 people and have had to find accommodation for the additional participants.They decided not to build a dedicated athletes' village in order to reduce costs. articles.title: Dylan Larkin Says Red Wings Trade Request Is Personal, Won't Reveal Reasons Behind Desired Move
articles.summary: Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin declined to explain the reasons behind his trade request when speaking to reporters Thursday for the first time since pursuing an exit from his team.
articles.body:
Former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin declined to explain the reasons behind his trade request when speaking to reporters Thursday for the first time since pursuing an exit from his team.

"There was a lot there, a lot of personal stuff... I'm going to try to be honest with you guys today, and I'm not ready to go there yet," Larkin said when asked why he requested a trade (h/t WXYZ Detroit's Alex Crescenti).

"I understand that there's answers that fans and people that care about this organization around the world want to know, but I'm really not ready to go there, and it's maybe something that I may never be."

The Red Wings announced Sept. 11 Larkin would attend training camp but not serve as captain this season.

The team later said Larkin would miss the beginning of camp with an upper-body injury.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 2 preview – Start/sit and more
articles.summary: Fantasy Football Advice - Rides, Fades, and Sleepers to help you set your lineup
articles.body:
Welcome to Week 2! Week 1 was a scoreboard-spinning bonanza — the highest scoring opening week in the Super Bowl era, with teams averaging almost 25 points per game. Wow. That barrage of offense translated to a ton of fantasy points. Sixteen players scored two of more touchdowns last weekend. Hopefully your team was in on the fun, and wasn't full of players who whiffed such as Matt Stafford, Drake Maye, Ja'Marr Chase, Jaylen Waddle, Kyle Pitts, Sr., and Colston Loveland.

For some, seeing those names in print might make you wince. Remember, it's just one week. Don't panic…yet.

You're getting a slightly abbreviated column this week. Sorry about that.

Chicago's 59 points was the second highest scoring output ever in a season-opening game. The Bears had 291 rushing yards, averaged 7.5 yards per carry, and scored six rushing touchdowns.

Chicago 59, Carolina 37 is a scorigami (first time ever for that final score), and at 96 points, the highest scoring Week 1 game in NFL history.

The Jets and Giants are both 1-0 for the first time since 2009.

Josh Allen now has nine career games with two of more rushing TDs plus two or more passing TDs. That's five more than anyone else in NFL history. He's also 20 th all time (among all players) in rushing TDs.

On Sunday, Derrick Henry had his 26 th game with 100+ rushing yards and multiple rushing TDs. That broke a three-way tie for most all-time (Jim Brown, LaDanian Tomlinson).

For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn't a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I'll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as "Rides" because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don't need me or anyone else telling you to start Jahmyr Gibbs . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column.

Each week, I'm picking a Ride, Fade ,and Sleeper of the Week . The rules: The Ride of the Week can't be a truly elite option, the Fade can't be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings.

This week, since the column is short, I'm doing two of each.

Last week, my Ride of the Week (Chris Olave – 182 receiving yards) and Fade of the Week (Drake Maye – 1 TD, 3 INTs) delivered. My Sleeper of the Week (mike Washington, Jr.) was OK, but not worth a spot in starting lineups.

D.J. Moore (vs. DET). If it ain't broke…I might just pick "No. 1 wide receiver going against the Lions" as my Ride of the Week all season, or at least until they get their starting safeties back. This contest has shootout written all over it, and like Olave last week, D.J. Moore is primed for a big game against this unit. He had 100 yards and a long TD last week against Houston's elite secondary, and should be able to build on that (and on his rapport with Josh Allen) against a defense that allowed the fifth-most fantasy points per game (FPPG) to opposing WRs last season. They'll be lucky if they aren't ranked worse than that by the time this season is done. Moore is listed as the RB13 this week and he's Top-10 for me.

Brock Purdy (vs. MIA). The extra rest from the Australia trip will do the 49ers good, although they might be itching to get back out there quickly after they dismantled the Rams so convincingly. This game shouldn't be competitive, but that won't stop Purdy from running it up early on an overmatched and very inexperienced Miami defense that just made Kirk Cousins look pretty good (although they did turn him over a couple of times, which kept the game closer than it should have been). He's got enough healthy weapons to light up Miami this weekend.

London was a sit for me last week, and as long as the Falcons' QB options are the pu pu platter of Cooper Rush and Tua Tagovailoa, I'm staying far away. The Panthers gave up 59 points last week, but most of the fantasy points went to Chicago's quarterback and running backs. Look for Atlanta to hand the Panthers a lot of Bijan Robinson. It's a good matchup for London, but I can't get past the abysmal QB situation.

Sam LaPorta (@BUF). LaPorta is always a volatile fantasy option, and in Week 1 he was just OK (5-48-0). His eight targets were encouraging, but this week's matchup is a horrible one and he'll probably need to find the end zone to give you a TE1 finish. The Bills were the single worst matchup for TEs last season (fewest catches, yards, and FPPG allowed), and they held Dalton Schultz in check in a Week 1 shootout (four catches for 35 yards)

Quentin Johnston (vs. LV) is listed as the WR30 this week and for me that's too low. No team suffered a bigger embarrassment in Week 1 than Jim Harbaugh's Chargers. Mike McDaniel's high octane offense struggled against an Arizona defense that everyone — and I mean EVERYONE — expected them to dominate. Ladd McConkey might miss this game. Look for a bounceback and a solid WR2 performance from Johnston in what now feels like a must-win game for the Chargers, who have a brutal schedule coming up.

Carson Wentz (@CHI). Yeah I know, it's Carson Wentz, who makes lots of mistakes and is now a career backup. I also know that he threw three TDs last week, has dangerous weapons at his disposal, and is facing a Bears' defense that just allowed four total TDs to Bryce Young. Ben Johnson is serious about setting the points record, so this could be another shootout. Any QB playing against Chicago's suspect defense warrants a look, and if you need a second QB in a Superflex this week, Wentz is a live play.

Going beyond the obvious elite options at each position, here a few more Rides for me this week:

QB: D. Prescott (vs. WAS), J. Daniels (@DAL), J. Dart (@LAR), P. Mahomes (vs. IND), B. Mayfield (vs. CLE), J. Love (@NYJ).

RB: K. Walker III (vs. IND), J. Williams (vs. WAS), K. Williams (vs. NYG), C. Hubbard (@ATL), J. Mason (@CHI), J. Croskey-Merritt (@DAL), and if you need to dig deep: K. Black (vs. MIA) and G. Holani (vs. ARI).

WR: G. Pickens (vs. WAS), C. Watson (@NYJ), G. Wilson (vs. GB), T. McLaurin and S. Diggs (@DAL), and if you need to go deep, D. Samuel, Sr. (vs. MIA), D. Vele (@BAL), and D. Wicks (@TEN).

TE: D. Kincaid (vs. DET), D. Goedart (@TEN), I. Likely (@LAR), and if you need someone from down in the rankings, T.J. Hockenson (@CHI), C. Okonkwo (@DAL), and A.J. Barner (@ARI).

Other Fades (among players who a lot of people might consider starting this week):

QB: J. Burrow (@HOU – not expecting anyone to sit him, but that defense is going to bounce back, so temper expectations), D. Maye (vs. PIT), M. Stafford (vs. NYG), D. Jones (@KC), J. Brissett (vs. SEA).

RB: B. Tuten (@DEN), Q. Judkins (@TB), J. Warren (@NE), M. Lloyd (@NYJ), T. Pollard (vs. PHI).

WR: J. Waddle (vs. JAC), D. Adams (vs. NYG), R. Odunze (vs. MIN), D.K. Metcalf (@NE), B. Thomas, Jr. (@DEN), M. Harrison (vs. SEA), C. Tate (vs. PHI).

TE: J. Johnson (@BAL), K. Pitts, Sr. (vs. CAR), B. Strange (@DEN).

articles.title: The myth of the Diamondbacks September ‘meltdown’
articles.summary: The myth Now, a heavily upvoted shitpost from the Diamondbacks subreddit, and a Tweet by one of the most toxic members of fandom may not seem worth bothering...
articles.body:
Now, a heavily upvoted shitpost from the Diamondbacks subreddit, and a Tweet by one of the most toxic members of fandom may not seem worth bothering about. And they probably are not. But it does reflect a general feeling that September is the cruelest month for Arizona fans. It is true that this is the fourth consecutive season where the team could be seen as imploding. There was the "backing into the post-season" meme from 2023, missing out by a narrow margin in 2024 and 2025, and while the story of this year has yet to be completed, at the time of writing the team is on the outside of the NL playoff picture. Never mind that their record would be winning two of the three divisions in the AL…

So, first stop. Is there any truth to the perception?

The team's performance in September over the past few years is not particularly better or worse than their performance the rest of the year. Indeed, the last time the D-backs had any kind of losing record in September was in 2022. Here's their performance by each calendar month since the beginning of the 2023 season:

The overall win percentage in that time is .521. Based on that, over the 3.5 seasons and 92 September games, you would expect their record in the month to be 48-44. It is actually… 47-45. If that's the "choking" demanded for the narrative, it's an underwhelming one. Now, I also hear, "The meltdown is when they need to win the last few games to make the wildcard they lose." So let's take a look at each recent season specifically, and see what actually happened.

2023 . Well, the above doesn't exactly support the idea of a meltdown, does it? On September 13, Arizona had just a 30.7% chance of making the post-season. But they were about to go on an 8-2 run which included sweeps against both the Cubs and Giants. The former was particularly huge. They came in to Chase Field on September 15, with a 2.5 game lead over the D-backs, and left three days later, behind Arizona and broken. Including that series, Chicago went 5-10 the rest of the way, and their odds cratered from 58% to zero in five days. Now that's what I call a genuine September meltdown. Losing the last four games, as the D-backs did? Irrelevant, as the subsequent playoffs proved.

2024 . This is the season where I would say there is the best case for a meltdown, and it's likely where the myth began. Though September as a whole was hardly a disaster, Arizona going 13-13. That, however, perhaps felt like a meltdown after the Diamondbacks went a stellar 35-17 in July and August. With seven games to go, the D-backs were three clear of the Braves. However, they'd lost the tie-breaker. Arizona went 2-5, while the Braves went 5-2, and the rest is history. But four of those games were against the Padres and Brewers , who were ahead of us in the standings. It included a loss by the odd run in nineteen in Milwaukee . A win there and the meltdown myth never gets started. That's the margin we're talking about here. Maybe we should be blaming the team which started 4-7 that year, not the one which finished 6-5.

2025 . For there to be a "meltdown" in September, I'd say there has to be a significant chance of success there to begin with. But the highest chance of the D-backs making the post-season that month was only 12.3%. The last day it was even twenty percent – still an outside shot – was back on July 19. Sure, as in 2023, they finished the year on a losing streak: five games this time. But also as there, that ignores the good run the Diamondbacks went on immediately before that, winning seven of nine. They'd have needed to go 4-1 thereafter to reach the playoffs, for an overall 11-3 record over the last couple of weeks. Not doing so, going "only" 7-7, is hardly a meltdown.

What I think is interesting is why some people choose to think the D-backs collapse, when the facts really don't particularly support that as a narrative. I think part of it is actually a back-handed compliment, in that this is the first time, literally in a generation, where the D-backs have been consistently competitive for several years in a row. Put it this way: nobody cares very much right now about September meltdowns over at Purple Row , despite the Rockies playing 42 points worse after August 31. Below, you'll see the team's winning percentage through 136 games, which is there or thereabouts around the end of August (save for 2020, when I used the number through 35 games).

The 2023-26 run is the first time the Diamondbacks has been above .450 (the line highlighted above), through that point in the season, for five consecutive seasons since 2003. It's the first time in over twenty years where Arizona have had four seasons in a row with meaningful baseball in the second half of this month. We're not used to having September baseball that matters . Or, at least, it seems to. The reality, of course, is that wins and losses count exactly the same. If you're looking for a reason why we "backed into the playoffs" in 2023, the 8-16 record of the D-backs in July is a far bigger explanation than anything in September.

Maybe fans remember failure better than success? Just ask Byung-Hyun Kim. Or this season, where we've had perpetual complaints about D-backs' LOBsters. They actually score a higher percentage of baserunners than 23 of the 30 MLB teams. Or demands the Diamondbacks do a better job with a man on third and less than two outs, when only three teams bring those runners home at a higher rate than Arizona. I'm not sure if it's a result of baseball being a game where a 30% success rate at hitting is considered elite, and 70% of baserunners will be stranded. It goes against studies which have shown team victories tend to be better remembered.

Yet here we are, some recalling meltdowns that barely happened. Of course, some people simply have a narrative to push, e.g. "Torey sucks!" and will make up whatever history they want to support it.

"My job is to get us to the playoffs. What happens after that is f___ luck." — Billy Beane

The reason he said that is because baseball has the biggest element of random chance in any of the major sports. The difference in the spot where ball meets bat, between a game-ending fly-ball and a game-winning home-run, is so small as to be beyond the bounds of human skill. Sure, some are better at it than others. But even Mark McGwire hit a home-run fewer than every ten at-bats. A baseball game is a series of chaotic and inherently unpredictable events. Over a season of 162 games, less so. But the smaller you shrink that, the greater the odds of something unexpected.

If we presume a 26-game month, there's a better than even chance that a .500 team will lose at least four games in a row. It's about a one-in-three chance for a five-game losing streak, so having one is basically meaningless in terms of "proving" anything. The problem is that, when a season comes down to the last few games, you're basically in "playoffs before the playoffs". Take 2025, where the D-backs would have needed to win four of the last five games to make it in. At that point, to quote Beane, what happens is "f___ luck". It's really not up to Torey very much. And you can expand the principle backwards.

The Diamondbacks are, let's be honest, not going to compete for the division title any time soon. The Dodgers simply have too many competitive advantages. From having the reigning MVP on their books for $2 million this year, to that Godzilla-sized television contract, alone worth more than all of the D-backs' revenue streams combined. While the scales of balance have the Dodgers' thumb pressing down on one side, all we can hope for is to compete for a wild-card spot. And four years in a row, Torey Lovullo has got us there, successfully negotiating the shoals of injury and MarteGate to have the team playing meaningful baseball into late September.

Maybe it's just me, but realistically, it's hard to demand anything more.

articles.title: Georgia Tech Football: Things I Think I Know – Mercer
articles.summary: A lighter in-state matchup after two weeks of tough competition
articles.body:
Well, that wasn't very fun. I know some people had faith in the upset, but Tennessee was just the better team. This week, we look ahead to Mercer , as they make the hour drive up from Macon to play the Jackets. Here is what I think I know as we look to win our first game in quite some time.

Mercer will not be as good as last season, but they still cannot be overlooked

Mercer was one of the premier programs in the FCS last season, finishing with a 9-3 record and a SoCon championship. They came into 2026 with high expectations, but a very different look. Head coach Mike Jacobs left the program to become the head coach at Toledo, and the Bears hired former Mercer defensive coordinator and West Georgia head coach Joel Taylor. Mercer also lost 2025 star quarterback Braden Atkinson , who left for Oregon State after throwing for 3,611 yards, winning the Jerry Rice Award as the top FCS freshman of the year, and winning the SoCon freshman of the year. Their best defensive lineman, Andrew Zock , also left with Coach Jacobs for Toledo. Needless to say, they had a lot to replace, but have started the year 2-1. This is a big thanks to quarterback Jaylen King and SoCon Preseason Offensive Player of the Year wide receiver Brayden Smith. He already has 284 yards this season, with over 130 yards in each of the first two games. He took a backseat in last week's loss against Furman, only racking up 21 yards, but he is still dangerous nonetheless.

Smith and this high-powered offense will be a test for the defense, as Mercer is not a team to be taken lightly. With how much the Jackets have struggled, we cannot be caught sleeping just because this is an FCS team. They have totaled 1,314 offensive yards this season, averaging 438 yards per game, including 219 rushing yards per game. Our run defense is currently sitting at 134th in the country, allowing 241 yards per game. This is exactly where we sat at last season, which is an unacceptable number for where we need to be to compete at a high level. I want us to keep improving and lock down this Mercer run game to instill confidence in our team.

Defensively, Mercer has been decent, but is still giving up 340 yards per game. I am praying that this is a much-needed week for the Jackets' offense, where they can return to fundamentals and focus on execution to help the team become more comfortable and confident. The offensive line also got pretty banged up last week, so this will be a good week for them to rest and give the younger guys more experience.

The offensive line is still a problem, and so is the offense as a whole.

While the offensive line certainly had its positive moments against Tennessee, there is still a lot of work to be done to restore the "physical and tough" identity that Brent Key once instilled in this group. Some of the struggles in this game were possibly due to injuries, as Ethan Mackenny, Jameson Riggs, and right tackle Malachi Carney all went down at some point on Saturday night. Those injuries affected the line, but they do not fully excuse the inconsistencies we saw up front.

The contrast from last season is especially glaring. The Jackets allowed Haynes King to be sacked just nine times all of last season, while Mendoza has already been sacked seven times through two games. The run game also tells a similar story. Through the first two games of last season, Georgia Tech had already racked up 543 rushing yards. This year, the Jackets only have 186. Yikes.

I will say, there were certainly flashes of progress against Tennessee, and it is impossible to overlook the fact that three offensive linemen had to leave the game. This group has a long way to go, but I do not think there is reason to panic just yet. Tech has had to replace a significant amount of production along the line, and we will see just how much they can improve throughout the season.

There were some bright spots on the offense, but going from the nation's top offense at one point last season to scoring our first offensive touchdown in the third quarter of Week Two is incredibly frustrating and embarrassing. Justice Haynes showed improvement against Tennessee, rushing for 81 yards while adding 36 yards receiving and two touchdowns. His heart, passion, and talent are evident, but the offensive line and play calling are not putting him in the position to succeed like we know he can.

One of the brightest spots against Tennessee was tight end Kevin Roche. He earned a PFN grade of 89.3 and turned in an impressive performance, hauling in six catches for 66 yards. His combination of size and athleticism gives this offense another weapon, and I hope that Key and Godsey keep him heavily involved.

I know there is a lot of criticism, and rightfully so. It is difficult not to feel frustrated watching this team struggle after seeing how high we climbed just a year ago. Still, there is plenty of football left to play. I hope Key and his staff can use this week to get back to the fundamentals, build confidence, and find the identity that made this team so successful last season.

The run defense played aggressively in the first half, but quickly dwindled in the second.

Injuries plagued the defense and definitely turned the tide of the game after Jaylen Mbakwe and Jordan Walker collided and suffered some pretty serious-looking injuries. Mbakwe was taken to Grady Hospital, but was thankfully released the following day with no major injuries reported. This is such a great reminder that life is bigger than football, and it is wonderful news to hear that he is doing ok.

Even though the final score does not reflect the effort on the field, I was overall happy (ish) with the defensive performance outside of the first drive and garbage time. The d-line showed flashes with some big stops and sacks in the first half, and then things started to dwindle later on in the game. I liked what I saw from the secondary as well, and I think they have great potential. It seems to be the same story for the Jackets, as we have a decent secondary but little ability to stop the run or get pressure on the QB. Safety Tae Harris once again was such a light for this team, as he earned a PFN grade of 95.0, which was the highest among all safeties in the country. Lineman Tawfiq Thomas had a good game for the Jackets, and I thought he was much improved from the Colorado game. Similar to the offense, I hope that the defense can heal and get some younger guys in the rotation against Mercer.

Special teams and penalties were much better.

After the special teams and penalties disaster against Colorado, things did look much better this past week. We had a blocked punt returned for a touchdown in the first quarter, all field goals were made, and operations overall seemed to run much more smoothly. We also went from nine penalties against Colorado to five against Tennessee, with a few of them questionable, in my opinion. This is a turn in the right direction.

After starting 0-2 for the first time since 1989 and going 1-6 in our last seven games, I am thankful that we get some easier competition this week to hopefully get things back on track. The reputation this team has built under Coach Key has now been shaken, and it could take a while for us to be taken seriously if we turn things around. Keep supporting and showing up for this team, and remember that it has only been two games, and we had a lot to replace and a lot of youth. Let's get things back on track this week and build confidence to carry into conference play.

articles.title: History says Cowboys can bounce back against the Commanders
articles.summary: There’s lots of reasons to be optimistic for the Cowboys to win this week
articles.body:
Week 1 didn't go according to plan for the Dallas Cowboys . A 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants leaves Dallas looking for its first win of the season, but there may not be many opponents Brian Schottenheimer's team would rather see coming through the doors of AT&T Stadium than the Washington Commanders .

Washington is also 0-1 after losing 24-22 to the Philadelphia Eagles , meaning Sunday's home opener already carries some extra importance. One NFC East team will leave the game 0-2.

We look at the reasons to be positive for this week's game.

The first reason to be positive about this game is Dak Prescott has owned Washington (we concede he also owned the Giants previously). Prescott has faced the Commanders 15 times in his career and has a remarkable 13-2 record. In those games he has thrown for 3,716 yards, 32 touchdowns against only five interceptions, with a 107.4 passer rating. That is already impressive, but his record against Washington when the game is played in Dallas is even better. Prescott is a perfect 7-0 at home against Washington.

Across those seven games he has completed 68% of his passes, thrown 20 touchdowns without a single interception, and produced a 126.4 passer rating.

Washington visited AT&T Stadium last October and Dallas hammered the Commanders 44-22. Prescott completed 21 of 30 passes for 264 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, finishing with a 130.4 passer rating. Dallas produced 409 yards of offense and scored on three of its four trips inside the red zone.

And it wasn't just Prescott who enjoyed that matchup. Javonte Williams rushed for 116 yards and a touchdown, averaging a whopping 6.1 yards per carry. CeeDee Lamb caught five passes for 110 yards and a touchdown, while George Pickens added 82 receiving yards.

Then there was Jake Ferguson . Ferguson caught all seven passes thrown his way and scored two touchdowns. Washington simply couldn't stop all of Dallas' weapons at the same time. That becomes especially interesting after what happened to Washington against Philadelphia on Sunday as tight ends seem to be the Commanders kryptonite.

Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert caught four passes for a team leading 77 yards and scored two touchdowns against the Commanders. One of those went for 43 yards. Jalen Hurts finished the game with three touchdown passes and no interceptions.

Ferguson therefore enters this game knowing both that he has already hurt Washington around the goal line and that Philadelphia just found success attacking the same defense with its tight end.

There are also positives Dallas can take from the Giants loss despite the final score. The biggest one came after halftime. Dallas only had two offensive possessions in the entire second half because New York controlled the clock for so long. The Cowboys scored a touchdown on both of them.

One was a 12-play, 75-yard drive finished by a Williams touchdown run. The next time Dallas got the football, Prescott quickly drove the offense down the field again and found Williams for a 17-yard touchdown reception. In other words, Dallas' offense finished the game by scoring touchdowns every time it touched the ball in the second half.

Williams also finished Week 1 with two total touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. CeeDee Lamb scored Dallas' other touchdown, while Prescott threw two touchdown passes.

The final offensive numbers were disappointing because Dallas simply didn't have the football enough, but there were signs late in the game that the unit was beginning to find a rhythm. If that continues into the home opener, Washington could have a difficult afternoon.

There were also flashes from the Cowboys' rebuilt defense that deserve attention.

Rookie safety Caleb Downs recorded his first NFL sack, blasting Jaxson Dart and forcing a fumble that New York recovered. Quinnen Williams then created Dallas' first takeaway of the season when he forced another fumble that Shavon Revel recovered. Those individual plays matter this week because Washington's offensive line is already missing its most accomplished blocker.

Five-time Pro Bowl left tackle Laremy Tunsil is on injured reserve after suffering a torn triceps. Washington has moved Brandon Coleman back outside to replace him. Defensive tackle Jer'Zhan Newton is also on injured reserve, as is cornerback Trey Amos . Tunsil's absence in particular gives Dallas' defensive front an opportunity.

The Cowboys didn't produce consistent enough pressure against New York, but Quinnen Williams showed that he can wreck a play, Downs showed Christian Parker is willing to send pressure from the secondary, and Dallas now gets to attack a Washington offensive line without its star left tackle .

Jayden Daniels also didn't exactly explode out of the blocks in Week 1. Against Philadelphia, Daniels completed only 18 of 34 passes, a completion rate of 52%, for just 164 passing yards. He did throw two touchdowns without an interception, but much of Washington's passing production arrived during its late comeback attempt. Dallas has also shown before that it can make Daniels uncomfortable.

The Cowboys don't need their rebuilt defense to suddenly become perfect. They simply need more of those disruptive plays and, most importantly, need to get off the field so Prescott and the offense have more opportunities.

Washington also came out of Week 1 with some new injury concerns.

Tight end Chig Okonkwo left the Philadelphia game with a hamstring injury, while linebacker Frankie Luvu and special teams standout Tyler Owens also suffered injuries. Their availability for Dallas will become clearer later this week.

Luvu's situation is particularly worth monitoring. He is one of Washington's most important defensive players and part of a pass rush that Dallas will need to account for with Tyler Smith still on injured reserve.

The final reason to be positive is that Dallas had to open its season on the road in a primetime divisional game. Now the Cowboys return to AT&T Stadium for their home opener, against an opponent Prescott has never lost to at home.

Washington, meanwhile, has to play its second consecutive divisional road game after beginning the season in Philadelphia. The Commanders go from Lincoln Financial Field straight into another difficult NFC East environment while Dallas gets its first home game of the year. That's an extremely tough condition for the Commanders to be in.

articles.summary: The Huskies' 2026-27 regular-season schedule is now complete following the release of the Big East schedule.
articles.body:
UConn women's basketball 's 2026-27 regular season schedule is complete.

The Huskies once again boast one of the most competitive nonconference schedules in the nation and will look to sweep Big East play for the fourth consecutive season.

The Big East announced its conference schedule Thursday afternoon, with tip times, TV and venue designation to be determined. UConn , which announced its nonconference schedule last month, begins conference play on Nov. 20, hosting Seton Hall , and will conclude the regular season on Feb. 28, hosting Butler.

The Huskies have won both the Big East regular-season and tournament crowns each of the past six seasons since rejoining the league in 2020. Last year, they defeated Villanova for the program's 24th Big East Tournament title.

The Big East announced a three-year extension with Mohegan Sun Arena in March to keep the conference tournament in Uncasville through 2029.

Heading into this season, UConn has won a program-record 70 straight Big East games, including conference tournament games - a streak that dates back to February 2023.

UConn finished the regular season undefeated last year for the first time in eight years.

That's expected to be a taller task this year.

Outside of Big East play, 10 of the Huskies' 12 nonconference opponents made the 2026 NCAA Tournament, including four of the Elite Eight participants and the national runner-up. UConn not only has dates set with rivals South Carolina , Tennessee and Notre Dame, but will face challenges against top-ranked teams, such as Michigan , Duke and LSU .

And for the first time in 33 years, UConn won't get a final nonconference test ahead of March Madness as the Huskies conclude their 2026-27 non-conference slate before New Year's Eve.

But even without a nonconference game during the thick of Big East play, the Huskies still have a packed schedule.

UConn will play three Big East games, including a visit to Villanova on Dec. 23, ahead of its annual holiday break in December. The Huskies return from the holidays and will once again close out the year playing on New Year's Eve (at Xavier). UConn opens 2027 on the road facing DePaul in Chicago on Jan. 3.

The Huskies will get two partial bye-weeks in January. First, a five-day break between a Jan. 13 home game vs. Marquette and a Jan. 18 game at Seton Hall. Then, a six-day break between its trip to South Orange, N.J., and its game at St. John's on Jan. 24.

UConn's final road game is scheduled for Thursday, Feb. 25, at Providence, while its last home game is Feb. 28 against Butler. Without home venue designations, it's unclear yet when the Huskies will celebrate their 2027 Senior Day, as the program honors its seniors during its last on-campus game of the year.

articles.title: Alex Bregman is having a monster second half
articles.summary: The Cubs offense is surging, led in part by their third baseman.
articles.body:
The Cubs took two of three from the National League East division-leading Braves at Wrigley Field, winning the series. Once again, likely NL MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong led the Cubs offense with two home runs and a triple, but as has often been the case this season he's had company with another teammate having a big game. On Wednesday night that backup act was Alex Bregman who put on an offensive show of his own [VIDEO] .

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video .

In addition to hitting his 26th bomb of the year, Bregman added a triple and a double on the night. It was just another great night at the ballpark for the 32-year-old third baseman who has a 5 fWAR season in his first year with the Cubs, the first such year for him since 2022. Bregman has really turned a corner since the All Star Break, as you can see from his splits below:

It's been a pretty big turnaround since mid-July for Bregman and it's mostly apparent on the power front. You can see that in both the Isolated Slugging (ISO) above but also just in the home run tally with Bregman almost doubling his home run total from the first half in 180 fewer plate appearances. But what really puts these numbers in perspective is the league context. Below you can see the top 15 players in MLB by fWAR since the All Star Break (is it any wonder the Cubs lead the league offensively with three guys in the top 15?):

Bregman hasn't just been good in the second half, he's been the best hitter in baseball by some metrics. The above chart is sorted by fWAR but if it were resorted by wRC+, a stat that measures hitters run production off a league and park normed baseline of 100, Bregman would rank first, followed by a virtual tie between Fernando Tatis, Jr. and PCA. Bregman is also pacing the field in wOBA, a fancy on-base percentage that gives hitters more credit for extra base hits.

Bregman hasn't just turned it on in the second half, he's returned to vintage Bregman. In fact, by the end of 2026 a glance at his slash line will show 2026 as his best season by fWAR since 2022. His process in scrutinizing his at bats and making adjustments is obvious to anyone watching him study the tape in the dugout after an at bat, but if you're more of a chart type you can also see the adjustment below:

You can see how Bregman's wOBA and ground ball rate are inversely correlated pretty clearly in this chart. As Bregman has hit the ball in the air more, he's gotten better production. The results speak for themselves [VIDEO] .

It's a good sign that the Cubs offense has kept rolling as they past the mid-point of September. With nine games left to play, they'll need Bregman, PCA and Seiya Suzuki to keep setting a torrid pace offensively as they try to out hit their pitching woes down the stretch and into the Wild Card round.

articles.title: Who is Forever Young? Meet the Japanese star of Belmont's Jockey Club Gold Cup and the richest racehorse in history.
articles.summary: Forever Young, the richest racehorse in history, is the star of the Jockey Club Gold Cup on Friday as Belmont Park reopens after 3 years of construction.
articles.body:
Belmont Park is reopening after three years and $455 million worth of renovations, with one of horse racing's biggest stars taking center stage.

Forever Young, the Japanese star who won last year's Breeders' Cup Classic, is the headline attraction for Belmont's return to racing on Friday. He's the star of a five-horse field - reduced from seven following the scratches of Banishing and Chunk of Gold - for the Grade 1, $1 million Jockey Club Gold Cup.

The Jockey Club Gold Cup, run at 1 ¼ miles on dirt, is the fifth race on Friday's Belmont card with a post time of 4:14 p.m. ET.

Before Forever Young steps into the starting gate, here's a guide to what you need to know about the Japanese star and his career.

A 5-year-old Japanese-bred son of Real Steel, Forever Young is one of the most accomplished racehorses on the planet and the sport's all-time leader in purse money won with more than $31 million in earnings.

Trained by Yoshito Yahagi, ridden by Ryusei Sakai and owned by Susumu Fujita, Forever Young has 11 wins, one second and three thirds in his 15 career starts. He beat Sierra Leone and Fierceness to win last year's Breeders' Cup Classic at Del Mar, and is a two-time winner of the $20 million Saudi Cup, the world's richest race.

When is Forever Young running at Belmont Park?

Forever Young is running in the Jockey Club Gold Cup on Friday, Sept. 18 at Belmont Park in Elmont, N.Y.

It's the fifth race on a nine-race card, and carries a post time of 4:14 p.m. ET.

Who is Forever Young facing in the Jockey Club Gold Cup?

Jockey Club Gold Cup horses, post positions, odds

Phileas Fogg (Gustavo Rodriguez, Kendrick Carmouche, 4-1)

Render Judgment (Kenny McPeek, Manny Franco, 20-1)

Forever Young (Yoshito Yahagi, Ryusei Sakai, 3-5)

What channel can I watch Forever Young in the Jockey Club Gold Cup on?

The Jockey Club Gold Cup will be shown on Fox.

Throughout Friday's Jockey Club Gold Cup card, racing will be shown on several of Fox's family of networks.

Has Forever Young ever raced in New York before?

No, the Jockey Club Gold Cup will be his first start in New York.

Has Forever Young raced in the U.S. before?

Forever Young has made three lifetime starts in the United States. He was third behind Mystik Dan and Sierra Leone in the 2024 Kentucky Derby, and third behind Sierra Leone and Fierceness in that year's Breeders' Cup Classic. His most recent race in the U.S. was the 2025 Breeders' Cup Classic, where he won by a half-length over Sierra Leone.

What races has Forever Young been in this year?

Forever Young has raced twice this year, both times in the Middle East. He won his second straight Saudi Cup in February, then finished second to American star Magnitude in the Dubai World Cup in late March.

His start in the Jockey Club Gold Cup will be his first in nearly six months as he prepares for another Breeders' Cup Classic start next month at Keeneland.

Where does Forever Young rank among the richest horses of all-time?

Forever Young is the sport's all-time leader in purse earnings by a wide margin, having secured more than $31 million in his 15-race career.

articles.title: Betting the Big Ten: Week 3 sees the start of Big Ten play
articles.summary: This week, we give our best bets for Michigan, USC, Oregon, Ohio State and every other team in the Big Ten Conference:
articles.body:
Week 2 started off horrendously as we missed on Friday night in the Rutgers matchup and a majority of the games in the noon slate on Saturday. However, we rallied back with an incredible afternoon slate as Mississippi State crushed Minnesota and Duke, Michigan State, and Maryland all covered.

We wrapped up a solid week at 9-7 and now sit at 16-18 on the year. One more good week and we'll be back above .500.

Week 3 is a bit of a dud on the schedule as only two Big Ten teams have games with spreads in the single digits. Maybe someone will surprise us.

All lines are courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. Please bet responsibly.

Portland State at Oregon (-57.5), O/U 67.5, 10:30 p.m. Friday

Oregon's start to the season has been shockingly bad, with a narrow win over a Group of 5 team and essentially a blowout loss to Oklahoma State. Unsurprisingly, the Ducks are 0-2 ATS on the year. Portland State, on the other hand, is 3-0 ATS. Who am I to bet against a trend like that?

Kent State at Ohio State (-52.5), O/U 59.5, Noon Saturday

Despite Ohio State's loss last week to now-No. 1 Texas, the Buckeyes actually covered the +1.5 spread. They are now 2-0 ATS on the season. However, the total is more appealing to me in this matchup. The Buckeyes hit the over in their only home matchup so far this season, and Kent State has gone over in both of their matchups so far as well. Give me the over.

Buffalo at Penn State (-41.5), O/U 50.5, Noon

This spread has shifted from 39.5 to 41.5 in recent days. While Penn State is just 1-1 ATS, Buffalo is 0-2 ATS and hasn't shown much sign of life. I'll take the Nittany Lions while it's still under six touchdowns.

Akron at Minnesota (-23.5), O/U 49.5, Noon

Vegas knows something in this matchup. The spread has dropped from 28.5 all the way down to 23.5 with no signs of stopping. A part of that may be due to the Golden Gophers' disappointing showing last week against Mississippi State, but I'm always one to follow the group.

Eastern Michigan at Wisconsin (-23.5), O/U 45.5, 12:30 p.m.

Both of these teams have been underwhelming ATS this year, with Eastern sitting at 1-2 and Wisconsin at 0-2. They've also gone under more often than not, as Eastern has hit the under in each of their three games while Wisconsin has gone over just once so far. I expect this game to be an ugly slog of a game, which leads me to the under.

Southern Illinois at Illinois (-38.5), O/U 54.5, 2 p.m.

The Fighting Illini have been a tad underwhelming to date, losing to Duke outright last week and being 0-2 ATS. The Salukis of Southern Illinois haven't been much better but they did cover last week. Throw in the fact that this line is creeping in Southern Illinois's favor, and I'm going to take a chance on the Salukis.

UTEP at Michigan (-35.5), O/U 49.5, 3:30 p.m.

Both of these teams are 1-1 ATS this season. Against the total, unsurprisingly, Michigan has gone under twice, as the offense has yet to kick it into gear. 35.5 feels awfully high to me for an offense that hasn't scored more than 17 points yet this season. I like the Wolverines to win comfortably, but until I see the offense have a breakout game, I can't pick Michigan to win by more than five touchdowns.

USC (-23.5) at Rutgers, O/U 59.5, 3:30 p.m.

The spread in this matchup has been all over the place. It started at 23.5, jumped up to 25.5, and has now settled back down to 23.5. I like USC to win this matchup with ease, but the Trojans are below .500 at covering the spread. Instead, I'm looking at the total. 59.5 seems very reasonable for these two offenses to surpass.

Western Kentucky at Indiana (-44.5), O/U 60.5, 4 p.m.

Curt Cignetti's Hoosiers continue their trend of playing absolutely no one in the non-conference. They've been massive favorites in each of their first two games but have failed to cover in both. I don't expect that to change.

Northern Iowa at Iowa (-40.5), O/U 49.5, 4 p.m.

The total is tough here as Northern Iowa has gone over twice while Iowa has gone under twice. Against the spread, both of these teams are an even 1-1 so this is a tough selection. I've been an unabashed hater of the Hawkeye offense but they've made me look silly most of this year. I'll give them the benefit of the doubt just this once.

North Dakota at Nebraska (-24.5), O/U 51.5, 7:15 p.m.

We have two excellent options to take in this matchup. Nebraska is 2-0 ATS while North Dakota is 1-2 ATS and 0-1 on the road. That in and of itself is a strong trend that makes me consider Nebraska -24.5. However, through these teams' combined five games, the over has hit each and every time. That's an even stronger trend. Give me the over.

Eastern Washington at Washington (-42.5), O/U 56.5, 7:15 p.m.

The total is untouchable in this matchup, as Eastern Washington has hit the over in each of their three games while Washington has only gone under. Washington has yet to cover as a favorite as well. While Eastern Washington isn't much better at 1-2 ATS, that one cover is about all we have to go off of.

Michigan State at Notre Dame (-29.5), O/U 52.5, 7:30 p.m.

I enjoy the fact that one of these two teams has to lose this game. The spread hasn't moved much since its initial release, and I think that's for good reason. Notre Dame is 2-0 ATS and has looked impressive while doing so. We don't know much about MSU just yet because they haven't played a Power Four team, but I tend to think that it's going to be a rough evening for the Spartans.

Colorado at Northwestern (-3.5), O/U 48.5, 7:30 p.m.

According to The Action Network, 77% of all bets are on Northwestern in this game. However, the spread has dropped from 5.5 to 3.5. This implies that there's big money on Colorado in this matchup. While the Buffaloes didn't cover a huge spread against Weber State last week, they looked very impressive winning outright as a 6.5-point underdog against Georgia Tech in Week 1. Give me Colorado.

Virginia Tech (-3) at Maryland, O/U 53.5, 7:30 p.m.

Both of these teams are undefeated ATS, with Virginia Tech covering against VMI and Old Dominion while Maryland covered large spreads against Hampton and UConn. I'll admit that I am making my pick here based on vibes alone, but I love the Hokies in this matchup. James Franklin had no trouble with Maryland when he was at Penn State. Given that Franklin imported a majority of his Penn State roster, I like Virginia Tech to cover.

The spread in this matchup has slid all over the place. It opened at UCLA -13.5, quickly shifted to 11.5, then plummeted to 16.5 in UCLA's favor. It has since settled back down to 14, but that is a ton of movement in a short amount of time. I like the Bruins in this game as they are 2-0 ATS against two solid opponents in Cal and San Diego State.
