articles.title: Ole Miss vs LSU: A Magnolia Bowl Preview
articles.summary: It's a matchup roughly nine months in the making, but at long last, we've finally made it. Week three of the college football season gives us Ole Miss vs. LS...
articles.body:
It's a matchup roughly nine months in the making, but at long last, we've finally made it. Week three of the college football season gives us Ole Miss vs. LSU , and this year it's a Magnolia Bowl with massive storylines. Number one is obviously former Rebel head coach Lane Kiffin returning to Oxford as the head coach of the Tigers, following his unceremonious departure in late November of last year. Expect Ole Miss fans to be less than hospitable to their former coach.

Then there's the potential College Football Playoff implications. Both of these teams have stacked rosters and hopes of making this year's playoff. A win Saturday would be a huge step in the right direction.

That being said, who has the edge, and what can we expect from both sides?

The opposite of what we're used to seeing with Kiffin-led teams, LSU's key to this one is defense. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker is one of the best in the sport, and likely a soon-to-be head coach.

But now his defense goes up against an Ole Miss offense with two possible Heisman candidates in Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy . And while the Rebel offense hasn't moved at breakneck speed this season, they've still shown the efficiency and explosiveness that we've all grown accustomed to seeing. If Princewill Umanmielen , Whit Weeks , and the rest of the Tiger defense can get into the backfield, slowing down the run and getting pressure on Chambliss, they'll be in good shape. The problem is that's easier said than done.

Then there's the offensive side of the ball, and a question of who plays quarterback this weekend. We all assume it will be Sam Leavitt , but with him being currently listed as doubtful, no one knows for sure. Is Leavitt legitimately injured, or is this another of Kiffin's well-known efforts at keeping things exciting?

Against a Rebel defense that has had problems this year, LSU is going to have to take shots downfield and see if they can force a few big plays by way of busted coverages in the secondary. That's the weakest part of the Ole Miss defense and the unit most susceptible to mistakes. Knowing that the Rebels' front seven is the strongest part of the defense and does a decent job of stopping the run, expect Kiffin and Charlie Weis Jr. to attack through the air early to see if they can open run lanes as the game progresses, both from the running backs, as well as designed quarterback carries.

How Does Ole Miss Keep Its Home Winning Streak Alive?

The Rebels have won 13 straight at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, but they're facing a huge test if they want to extend that streak to 14.

For Ole Miss, it'll have to start with defense. So far this season, they've been less than stellar. But with Antonio Kite and Sharif Denson both expected back, things should improve down the stretch. They're expected to face a quarterback in Sam Leavitt who has been turnover-prone this season. Last week in a win over Louisiana Tech, Leavitt threw three interceptions in the first half. For the Rebels, that means they have to find a way to make Leavitt beat you with his arm. Keep him from escaping the pocket, and make him make accurate throws in tight windows. If they can do that, they put a dent in the Tigers' offense.

Then there's the offense. Starting off, Chambliss has to make smart decisions and be accurate with the football. If he can get the ball to playmakers like Deuce Alexander and Horatio Fields on the outside, it could free up space for Lacy to find openings up the middle.

Then there's the Rebel offensive line. While they've been pretty good in pass protection this season, this is going to be their toughest test yet. As for run blocking, they've struggled at times to get to the next level, especially with speed, which will definitely have to improve if they want to succeed running the ball against the Tigers.

This just feels like a game that's going to come down to defensive execution. Both offenses are likely going to have some success, which brings this down to which defense can make a timely stop when it's most needed. And so far this season, the answer to that question has been LSU. Until we see something from the Rebels to prove otherwise, that has to be the way we lean in this matchup.

Both rosters are loaded on both sides of the ball, but the Ole Miss defense has looked extremely shaky so far this year. So while the atmosphere surrounding Oxford should help the Rebels, as it's going to be a madhouse, take Kiffin and the Tigers to ultimately leave with a massive road win in what should be a wildly exciting, close, tense matchup.

articles.title: Panthers DC Ejiro Evero talks about receiving criticism after allowing franchise-record 59 points
articles.summary: Panthers DC Ejiro Evero talked with reporters for the first time since his unit allowed a franchise-record 59 points in Week 1.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero has been far from the most popular man in Charlotte over the past handful of days. But that's what comes with the territory, especially after your unit allows nearly 60 points in front of the home crowd.

On Sunday, the Panthers surrendered a franchise-record 59 points in their season-opening loss to the Chicago Bears . Despite putting up an impressive 37 points of their own, Carolina was doomed in by their overwhelmed defense—which allowed Bears quarterback Caleb Williams and company to run wild all afternoon.

By game's end, Chicago tallied a ridiculous 552 yards of total offense and eight touchdowns. Much of that damage came through the ground, where the Bears rushed for 291 of those yards and six of those scores.

Evero, who spoke with reporters for the first time since the nightmarish performance, was asked what his defense must do better to tighten up moving forward.

"We gotta play blocks better upfront. There's some thing we can do better schematically," Evero stated on Thursday. "We gotta get in better condition. I think there's a lot of factors there, but we feel like they're all correctable."

Expectations were relatively high for the Panthers defense entering the 2026 campaign. In addition to going from the 32nd-ranked group in 2024 to the 16th in 2025, Carolina signed pass rusher Jaelan Phillips and Pro Bowl linebacker Devin Lloyd to big-money deals out of free agency in the spring.

They, obviously, didn't deliver on those expectations right away—and Evero understands the vitriol from it all. He was later asked about dealing with the criticism coming off the defeat.

"Gotta have it both ways, right?" he replied. "When things go well, I get a lot of praise. When things don't, I don't.

"And I get that part of it. That's fine. But it doesn't really matter. We have to continue to just find a way to get better, and that's the objective."

Week 2 will present Evero and the defense with a pretty good chance at getting better—as they'll travel to face the Atlanta Falcons (and whoever they're starting under center) on Sunday.

articles.title: Does the Bills' new Highmark Stadium have a roof? What to know
articles.summary: The Bills’ $2.2B stadium is open-air with a canopy roof, not a dome. Here’s how it’s designed to protect fans and keep Buffalo’s identity.
articles.body:
Snow, wind, and freezing cold have always defined Buffalo football. The Bills' new stadium will keep that identity intact without building a dome.

The $2.2 billion project is in Orchard Park across Abbott Road from the old Highmark Stadium .

While some NFL teams have opted for fully enclosed domes or retractable roofs, the Bills ' new home is open-air, with a partial canopy designed to shield fans from the worst of the weather while still letting the elements play their role.

How much of the new Highmark Stadium is covered?

Step inside the Bills’ new home with a visual tour of Highmark Stadium

The new stadium features a steel canopy that covers about 64% of all seating. The roof is designed to:

Amplify crowd noise by reflecting sound back onto the field.

Improve comfort in one of the NFL's harshest winter climates.

A sacred goodbye for Bills fans: Inside Highmark Stadium's final season

How does the canopy snow-melt system work?

Buffalo's canopy isn't just big. It's high-tech. Engineers describe it as the largest and most advanced snow-melt system in the world.

Hydronic heat pipes run throughout the steel decking, circulating warm fluid to melt snow and ice.

Sensors automatically trigger the system when snow accumulates.

Concave shape helps collect precipitation so it can melt quickly.

This design is intended to reduce dangerous snow buildup and improve safety during heavy lake-effect storms. The canopy does not extend over the playing field, which means snow, rain and wind can still affect games.

The dome debate has swirled for decades. Here's why leaders and the team chose open-air instead:

Tradition: The Bills are synonymous with tough-weather football.

Cost: A full dome or retractable roof would have added hundreds of millions more to the project.

Fan experience: Ownership has emphasized that Buffalo's outdoor atmosphere is unique and should be preserved.

Unlike the current Highmark Stadium, which uses synthetic A-Turf Titan, the new field has natural grass.

A SubAir system manages soil moisture, aeration, and field heating.

Grow lights keeps the grass healthy during long Buffalo winters.

Will there still be snow games in Buffalo?

Step inside as the old Highmark Stadium is torn down piece by piece

Yes. While the canopy shields most fans, the field itself will remain exposed to the elements. Snow and wind could still play a factor, keeping Buffalo's reputation for wild-weather games intact.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian addresses the team’s controversies surrounding Holly Rowe
articles.summary: The Texas head coach admitted that how he handled his post-game interview directly contributed to Arch Manning’s Monday comments.
articles.body:
The discourse surrounding the lack of in-game or post-game interview from Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian on Saturday when his team overcame a 21-point deficit to beat the then-No. 1 Ohio State Buckeyes in Austin erupted into a full-fledged national controversy on Monday when quarterback Arch Manning called an AI video of Sarkisian slapping ESPN reporter Holly Rowe "hilarious."

The controversy heightened over the 24 hours between Manning's insensitive comments and his public apology issued to Rowe , who quickly accepted it publicly following a private conversation with the Texas quarterback.

During a Thursday Zoom interview with reporters, Sarkisian finally addressed both situations four and a half days after the game ended, first re-hashing the technical difficulties reporter Laura Rutledge addressed on the broadcast.

"I had to make an in-moment decision to say wait on the interview or try to get with our team and try to make the proper adjustments to come out and play as good as we could in the second half. I let Laura know that, and I think she said that on air," Sarkisian said. "And then I had an opportunity to visit with Laura when we came back out of the locker room to let her know where our thoughts were as a team and what we needed to do in the second half of that game."

After the game, Rowe was visibly annoyed when Sarkisian cut short her attempt at an interview by saying, "That's Texas fight, hook 'em," and walking off to join his team to sing the school's alma mater, leaving a school spokesperson to tell The Athletic that technical difficulties continued, forcing a fan site to scour the broadcast in an attempt to determine how long Sarkisian waited with Rowe before walking off.

"As it pertains to after the ball game, there was a delay after I greeted Coach [Ryan] Day in the middle of the field. There was a delay in the moment. Through that delay, I wanted to go celebrate with our team. We just had a 21-point fourth-quarter comeback against the No. 1 team in the country. If hindsight's 20/20, if I could do it all over again, I would have exuded more patience in that moment and sat through and waited for the interview with Holly," Sarkisian said.

"Obviously, we have a ton of respect for ESPN and Holly. Holly and I go way back even to my days of playing at BYU, and we've got a great relationship. ESPN is a great partner of ours. We know we're going to have more opportunities with that crew covering us, and we're looking forward to those opportunities. So, could have definitely handled that situation better with a little bit more patience in the moment."

The Texas head coach then acknowledged that his handling of the post-game interview with Rowe resulted in the creation of the AI video that Manning saw and reacted to during his Monday press conference.

"That obviously led to the situation with Arch and his press conference as it pertained to the AI video, and obviously Arch recognizes he made a mistake, and it's an unfortunate one," Sarkisian said. "Nowhere do we condone domestic violence or violence against women. Nothing in our program says that, nor Arch individually. I think if he could take it back, he would. But he has since apologized to Holly. He's made a public apology, and our goal is that we can move forward and him be the guy that we all know that he is and what he represents."

With the rapid advancement of technology enabling the creation of AI videos by anyone, Sarkisian spoke with his team about the need to be "more conscientious with our word choice."

"Although we can think of something as kind of satire or fun, at the same token, that has a direct effect on other people. I've seen AI videos about me that aren't very welcoming. Some of them I laugh at, some are like, 'Ooh, that that stings a little bit,' but that's the world we live in today. And so, just acknowledging that from a players and coaching staff perspective, and then our choice of words and how we acknowledge or don't acknowledge those things, I think moving forward is very important," Sarkisian said.

For Manning, who has a multi-million dollar brand to protect and his family's hard-earned reputation to uphold, it's a moment from which he and the Longhorns are ready to learn from and move on from as they take the field for the first time this season as the nation's top-ranked team.

"I think he obviously feels bad about the situation, but the same token, I don't think it was a malicious statement by him. I think that was not the intent by any means, and so I think at his core he knows what he believes in and what he stands for. Like I said, he's had a good week of work. I think he's excited to get back on the field and play," Sarkisian said.

"But also, I think it's a good reminder of what we represent and the brand that we represent here at the University of Texas. The amount of coverage our program gets, more so than ever when you're the No. 1 team in the country, we're going to get scrutinized for all that we do. And so, being mindful of that, I think, is important for all of us."

articles.title: Astros Gold Glove OF acquired from Blue Jays has tanked his free agent value
articles.summary: This outfielder's free agent value has dropped considerably.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are going to have a lot of changes made to the team this upcoming offseason. A few players will be traded, and others will hit the open market and likely walk.

One of those players set to be a free agent is Gold Glove outfielder Daulton Varsho , whom the Astros got from the Toronto Blue Jays at the MLB trade deadline.

Unfortunately for Varsho, however, is that he's completely tanked his free-agent value. As CBS Sports' Matt Snyder pointed out, Varsho's struggles this season, especially since joining the Astros, have likely ruined his value this offseason.

Daulton Varsho has tanked his free agent value this year

"He's been worse since the trade to Houston, hitting just .179 with a 53 OPS+ and -0.1 WAR," Snyder writes. "He wasn't a star, but he looked after last season like stardom might be possible. Now he's barely playable."

Varsho will be heading into his age-30 MLB season next year, and it's likely to be on a new team, as he's been a major letdown for the Astros this season since the trade.

In 38 games, he has -0.1 bWAR with a 53 OPS+ and a .540 OPS. In 99 games with the Blue Jays before the trade, he had 0.8 bWAR with a .682 OPS and 87 OPS+.

Even though he was better in Toronto than he's been in Houston, his overall season production has been a major step back from his 121 OPS+ 2025 season with the Blue Jays.

He's regressed significantly and has likely tanked his value on the open market. His defense isn't as good as before, and his offense is well below league average.

It's going to be hard for Varsho to land a deal of any substance this offseason. More likely than not, he's going to be forced to take a cheaper one-year prove-it deal.

After a strong 2025 season, his production in 2026 has been a massive letdown. Varsho has tanked his free-agent value this year, and now he is going to miss out on a chance to land a huge contract in his first year as a free agent.

articles.title: Breaking down advanced stats from the Chicago Bears' Week 1 victory
articles.summary: After their offensive explosion in Week 1, where do the Chicago Bears stack up from an analytics perspective?
articles.body:
Given how things transpired for the Chicago Bears in their 59-37 victory over the Carolina Panthers in Week 1, just about any number on the stat sheet was going to land in their favor. From the more standard point-of-view, that's widely reflected in their counting stats. It starts to look even better, though, when we move into the more advanced end of the statistical spectrum.

From the standpoint of more traditional numbers, the Bears ' 59 points and 552 yards of total offense each top the league after the opening week. Their 271 yards rushing also sit atop the league's offensive groups, with D'Andre Swift's 124 and Kyle Monangai 's even 100 ranking fourth & seventh, respectively. Caleb Williams ' 269 yards through the air ended up in eighth.

Again, the regular ol' stats to which we are accustomed certainly do the Bears justice. But the advanced stats love them all the same.

Photos from Bears' historic 59-37 win over Panthers in Week 1

At +0.41, the Bears led Week 1 in offensive EPA per play. They also finished third in passing EPA per dropback (+0.54) and sixth in explosive-pass rate (12.9 percent). Unsurprisingly, each of their rush EPA per play (+0.38) and rush yards over expected per attempt (+3.07) blew everybody else out of the water. Kansas City finished second in the former (+0.22) while San Francisco came in as the no. 2 team behind the Bears in the latter, at +1.41.

Given all of that, it comes as no surprise that the Bears had their two running backs in the top 10 in individual EPA per attempt, with Swift at +0.51 (2nd) and Monangai at +0.25 (10th). In the passing game, Williams landed in fourth in EPA per dropback (+0.45), with each of Jahdae Walker (+1.38), Rome Odunze (+1.34), and Cole Kmet (+1.19) finishing in the top 25 in EPA per target.

As inspiring as the offensive collective and the individual standouts were on the offensive side, the Bears did have some visible issues on defense. Just like the success of the offense allows the eye test and the analytical side to play off of one another, the defensive side plays out much the same.

The 478 yards they allowed were the third-most in Week 1, with the 37 points surrendered to Carolina serving as the fourth-highest. Sure enough, that's also reflected in the advanced stats. The Bears allowed +0.21 EPA per play in total, which was eight-worst among the league's defense. That was probably evident given that, in general, you want a minus in front of the defense's EPA rather than the plus that indicates offensive success. Each of the pass EPA per dropback (+0.31) and EPA per rush attempt faced (+0.06) were in the bottom 10, as well.

It's important to note that coming off just one week of play, though, the analytics landscape is pretty simple. Samples are too small to make any clear declarations or showcase any real tendencies, both of which will continue to add context to these numbers as the season progresses. That's probably especially true on defense, where the rotation at various levels is still in need of sorting and leaves the sample even lower virtually across the board. As the sample grows, a number of other factors come into play beyond EPA.

Nevertheless, the Bears' advanced statistical output in Week 1 should serve as a pretty nice springboard toward being regular darlings in the analytics game throughout 2026 on offense while continuing to offer some cause for concern on the other side of the ball.

articles.title: ‘I’m Russian’: NHL star Ovechkin defends Putin ad appearance
articles.summary: Washington Capitals captain under fire for appearing in an election campaign video for Putin’s United Russia party.
articles.body:
Alexander Ovechkin ⁠has said he agreed to appear in a political campaign advertisement for the United Russia party, which is backed by Russia’s President Vladimir Putin, because ⁠he supports his country.

“I’m Russian, and I support my country,” Ovechkin, the all-time leading goal scorer for the National Hockey League (NHL) in North America, told reporters at the Washington Capitals’ media day on Thursday.

“I’m for peace ⁠and love, and I hope in the world it doesn’t matter who you are; I hope everybody understands, everybody wants peace, and everybody hopes everything is going to be OK in the world.”

Russia will hold a parliamentary election from September 18 to ‌20, the first since it launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022.

Ovechkin, who can be seen standing behind Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov in the video, said he was asked to participate and did not hesitate to agree. He added that he will live in Russia following the end of his sports career.

“As soon as I’m done playing hockey, I’m probably going ⁠to stay there,” he said. “I’m gonna live there, my kids ⁠gonna live there, family. I’m for peace and love, and I hope everything’s going to be OK.”

Ovechkin has faced scrutiny over his long-standing ties to Putin as Russia wages war in Ukraine. In ⁠2017, he formed a public movement in support of Putin, and his Instagram profile picture is a photo of ⁠him and the Russian president.

He called for peace ⁠in February 2022 following his home country’s invasion of Ukraine. When asked about his support for Putin at the time, he said: “Well, he is my president. But … I am not in politics. I am ‌an athlete and … I hope everything is going to be done soon.”

Ovechkin, who turned 41 on Thursday, has scored 929 goals in 1,573 regular-season NHL games, ‌and ‌the upcoming season will be his 22nd in the league. He led the Capitals to a Stanley Cup in 2018.

He considered retirement after the Capitals missed the playoffs last season, but said he was lured back by off-season moves he felt made Washington a Stanley Cup contender once again.

“The new faces we have give us a chance to fight for a Cup,” Ovechkin said.

“If it was truly a rebuild, it would be hard for me.”

articles.title: Seattle Torrent welcomes Brett Sonne as assistant coach
articles.summary: The Seattle Torrent has completed its coaching staff for the 2026-27 Professional Women’s Hockey League season, hiring Brett Sonne as an assistant coach.
articles.body:
The Seattle Torrent has completed its coaching staff for the 2026-27 Professional Women's Hockey League season, hiring Brett Sonne as an assistant coach.

Following the team's inaugural season, the Seattle Torrent parted ways with its head coach, Steve O'Rourke, and promoted former assistant coach Christine Bumstead to the helm.

Sonne joins Bumstead and assistant coach Stefanie McKeough behind the bench as the team prepares for its second season.

"We are excited to introduce him to Seattle," General Manager Meghan Turner said in a statement, praising Sonne's professional playing background and coaching experience.

The British Columbia native brings five seasons of junior hockey coaching experience. Most recently, he served as an assistant coach with the Coquitlam Express of the British Columbia Hockey League. Before that, he spent three seasons with the Ridge Meadows Flames, helping guide the team to its first league championship in 26 years during the 2023-24 season.

"I'm thrilled to have the opportunity to join the Torrent organization," Sonne said. "I'm looking forward to building relationships with the players and staff and helping this team succeed."

Before moving into coaching, Sonne enjoyed a lengthy professional playing career. He played four seasons with the Western Hockey League's Calgary Hitmen and was selected by the St. Louis Blues in the third round of the 2007 NHL Draft. He was named WHL Player of the Year in 2009 and won a gold medal with Team Canada at the 2009 World Junior Championship.

Sonne later spent four seasons in the American Hockey League, primarily with the Peoria Rivermen, before continuing his career overseas through 2019. He began coaching shortly after retiring from professional hockey.

articles.title: Texas Tech's Joey McGuire has weird feel about Friday home game on `holy ground’ for Texas preps
articles.summary: Joey McGuire often has roamed a sideline during games in Texas on Friday nights in the fall. This time will feel much different for the Texas Tech coach.
articles.body:
Joey McGuire often has roamed a sideline during games in Texas on Friday nights in the fall. This time will feel much different for the Texas Tech coach.

The 13th-ranked Red Raiders, the defending Big 12 champions, play their conference opener in prime time against No. 22 Houston. It will be Tech's first regular-season home game on a Friday since 1941.

"It's weird because I'm so used to Friday nights in the state of Texas is kind of holy ground when it comes to Texas high school football," said McGuire, the fifth-year Tech coach who won three state championships while head coach at Cedar Hill High School near Dallas from 2003-16.

Even before the Big 12 released a list of non-Saturday games in April, Texas Tech regents chair and billionaire booster Cody Campbell had heard about the plans to move his school's conference opener. He posted on social media that "Friday Night Lights are sacred in the Great State of Texas!" and also wrote that it was "absolutely absurd" that the Big 12 and Fox Sports would consider that.

But the Big 12 television contract allows for 12 regular-season football games a year to be played on a day other than Saturday.

Big 12 Commissioner Brett Yormark, who had some public back-and-forth with Campbell, has said that television ratings for the conference's Friday night games last season were 64% better than its average rating.

This isn't the only non-Saturday game for Texas Tech

The Red Raiders (2-0) have two non-Saturday regular-season games this year. Their regular season finale at home against TCU is on Thanksgiving night. In their previous 30 seasons in the Big 12, they played only six times on Friday, all on the road and with four of those coming the day after Thanksgiving. The last was in 2023.

"Well, obviously people have known for a long time that you play high school football in the state of Texas on Friday night," McGuire said. "And so this is a little different, but it's huge."

This meeting of expected contenders is the first of eight games matching Big 12 teams that won't be on a Saturday. Five of those are in November. Eleven of the league's 16 teams will be part of those conference games.

Houston (2-0), which played three Friday night games last season, and Texas Tech are among five teams that will play two this year. The Cougars are at Colorado on Nov. 13.

Another sellout near where `Friday Night Lights' began

Even playing on a Friday night, this will be Tech's 10th consecutive home sellout.

"That was one of the things that I was definitely worried about, even though we have the best fan base in the country," McGuire said. "But we're also in Friday Night Lights, like the world of Friday Night Lights in West Texas. That's where it all began whenever you think about the book and everything like that. But it's going to be a great game."

The Texas Tech campus in Lubbock is a little more than two hours north of Odessa, Texas, where the 1988 Permian High School team was the subject of Buzz Bissinger's book "Friday Night Lights" that was released in 1990.

That was adapted into a 2004 feature film starring Billy Bob Thornton as the coach. A television series with that title had a five-season run from 2006-11.

McGuire remains a big supporter of Texas high school coaches

McGuire is a member of the Texas High School Coaches Association (THSCA) Hall of Fame, and the Texas High School Football Hall of Fame. He constantly refers to Texas Tech as the unofficial home of the THSCA, and 11 members of his current staff have ties to the organization. He regularly speaks at the group's annual convention and hosts clinics for high school coaches each year.

During pregame Friday night, McGuire plans to wear his THSCA cap to show support for all prep coaches and that organization.

articles.title: Leics make good start chasing 334 to beat Hants
articles.summary: Leicestershire and Hampshire's fight to avoid relegation from Division One will head into day four after the Foxes closed on 156-3, chasing 334 to win.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Uptonsteel Grace Road, Leicester (day three)

Hampshire 214 & 363: Gubbins 133; A Patel 4-103

Leicestershire 244 & 156-3: Ahmed 55; Currie 1-27

Leicestershire (3 pts) need 178 more runs to beat Hampshire (3 pts)

Leicestershire and Hampshire's fight to avoid relegation from Division One will head into day four of their game at Uptonsteel Grace Road after the Foxes closed on 156-3, chasing 334 to win.

Earlier, Hampshire had been bowled out for 363 in their second innings, of which Nick Gubbins made 133. Ajaz Patel took 4-103 and Ian Holland 3-37 as Leicestershire's most successful bowlers.

There is plenty at stake. A draw sends both counties down but, assuming a positive result, the losing side will be confirmed as relegated to Division Two with the winner taking a mathematical chance of survival into the final week of the County Championship season, albeit tenuous in both cases.

After the hammer blow of the 27-point sub-standard pitch penalty announced on Wednesday, Leicestershire's would depend not only on winning away to title contenders Warwickshire but in doing so taking 20 points more than Essex pick up from their trip to Glamorgan.

Hampshire's task if successful here would be easier, if only marginally so, first requiring them to beat Sussex at home, and again assuming minor gains by Essex in Cardiff.

Given the news overnight, with Leicestershire's stay in Division One hanging by a thread after just one season, few spectators would have been surprised had Hampshire merely added to the punishment.

Yet competitive instincts reasserted themselves. Nightwatcher Manny Lumsden, leg before on the sweep, was the only casualty in the first 40 minutes, but once the new ball was available, things began to happen. Winning a place in Sunday's One-Day Cup final line-up was another incentive.

Holland needed only six deliveries to make an impact as Gubbins, who had added just nine to his overnight 124, edged to second slip. Ben Green induced a leading edge to mid-on from Ben Brown and was unlucky not to find more success during a testing spell.

Tom Scriven found late movement to remove Joe Weatherley before Ajaz Patel struck twice with his left-arm spin, Ben Mayes edging to slip and Scott Currie hoicking to mid-on, giving the New Zealand international four wickets in a Leicestershire shirt for the first time.

When Holland had James Fuller palpably leg before, raising the Leicestershire's captain tally to nine wickets in the match, Hampshire had lost their last six for 80 runs.

With time on their side, Leicestershire could afford to be risk averse and by tea had cut the target to 258 with 32 overs left in the day and potentially another 96 on Friday.

The one wicket to fall had been that of Rishi Patel, caught behind off Currie's lovely late away-swinger. Patel will be a Hampshire player next season, so this was his last innings on the ground in a Leicestershire shirt.

Hampshire's second breakthrough came 10 overs after tea as Sheridon Gumbs, having built patiently to that point, launched Felix Organ's off-spin for six over long off, but then reached for a ball that spun away from him and hit straight to short extra cover.

Rehan, whose eight fours included some lovely shots square or behind square on the off side, completed a half-century from 78 balls. He was dropped without addition, Lumsden not quite managing to hold on to a difficult chance square on the leg side, but had added only five more when Lumsden himself had him caught at slip. Bad light brought a close with six overs lost.

articles.title: 'Built differently' - Hodgkinson reveals hamstring abnormality
articles.summary: Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson says she is "built differently" after an MRI scan uncovered an "abnormality" in her hamstring.
articles.body:
Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson says an MRI scan has uncovered an "abnormality" in her hamstring.

Following a suspected tear last year, Hodgkinson had a scan which revealed she has a "split" hamstring, giving her two tendons instead of one.

The 24-year-old is still learning how to manage the anomaly, which allows her to continue running when one of the tendons is torn but may also make her more susceptible to breakdowns.

Following her second-place finish to Swiss Audrey Werro in the 800m final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest in September, Hodgkinson announced she had sustained another hamstring tear at the European Championships in Birmingham a few weeks earlier.

"My body is quite literally built differently," said Hodgkinson. "Where most people have one tendon, mine is split - I have two - and we're trying to figure out if it's a strength or a weakness.

"So when one of them tore, I still had another one because it's split. In Birmingham, it didn't affect me during the race, but I could feel something wasn't quite right.

"It's a weird one. You can still run on them. I haven't missed any training the last three weeks. But I've just had to alter my approach. I've had to take my foot off the speed [training], because that's when it's most risky."

Hodgkinson has endured two injury-plagued seasons since winning Olympic gold in Paris in 2024, waiting for more than a year to race again after suffering a hamstring injury the following February.

Impressing on her return in August 2025 with back-to-back Diamond League wins, she went on to set a new indoor 800m world record in February 2026 before winning gold at the World Indoor Championships a month later.

However, she has been unable to replicate that form outdoors, suffering three defeats by Werro, including losing her European crown to the 22-year-old.

Hodgkinson has since said she suffered a freak injury while jogging along a canal during a warm-down session, sustaining cuts to both knees and whiplash-like jarring in her back which have made the past few months a "battle".

But, while acknowledging that the fall could have contributed to her injury at the European Championships - which ruled her out of Diamond League meets in Zurich and Brussels - she stressed she is not making excuses.

"Part of me wants to talk about it and then part of me doesn't, because I feel like my words get twisted or people are like 'oh, she's making excuses'," Hodgkinson said.

"Going into the Europeans, I thought I was in the best shape ever. But when I fell over, that kind of messed me up way more than I thought it did. I think that's what contributed to my hamstring, because I couldn't really use my quad for a while."

Speaking after her defeat by Werro at the Ultimate Championship, Hodgkinson described 2026 as "frustrating" but remained optimistic: "Overall, I'm finishing second in the world and I can't really be too hard on myself for that."

Hodgkinson will end her 2026 season in London at the all-female Athlos event, launched by Reddit founder Alexis Ohanian, on Friday.

articles.title: Liverpool gifted chance to secure £73m discount before January
articles.summary: Liverpool's start to the season has left many supporters confused about the direction of the team. The summer saw a change in management, with Andoni Iraola...
articles.body:
Liverpool 's start to the season has left many supporters confused about the direction of the team.

The summer saw a change in management, with Andoni Iraola taking the reins at Anfield, and the Reds have somewhat struggled to deliver so far under the Spaniard.

The players' abilities to battle adversity on the pitch seems to have improved since Arne Slot's tenure, but the squad still looks incomplete and there is work to be done in the January window.

After another massive outlay in the summer, budget constraints could restrict the Reds' winter window, but a £75 million discount could be the perfect business for Iraola's team.

Liverpool can finally sign £73 million attacker five years on

Jadon Sancho is a name that once would have had many of the Anfield faithful excited, but the Englishman's career has veered off the astronomical path it was on only five years ago.

When the then 21-year-old left Borussia Dortmund in 2021, Liverpool were heavily rumoured to be interested in a move for the winger – with Jurgen Klopp reported to be a big admirer.

The Englishman opted to join Manchester United for £73 million that summer however, and now after a couple of disappointing seasons at Old Trafford and three loan moves away from The Red Devils the 26-year-old finds himself as a free agent.

Now, faced with a lack of attacking options in the squad, it could make sense for Iraola to bring in the man that Liverpool almost signed for £73 million for free.

Sancho made 39 appearances for Aston Villa last season, helping them to a Europa League title and a fourth-place finish in the league.

Although the Englishman was far from his best, he was consistently involved at the West Midlands club, being deployed on both the left and right wings.

Liverpool currently lack clear options on the right side of their attack with the solution seemingly being to play other forwards out of position, so the addition of Sancho, who has a wealth of topflight and European experience, would be a very sensible move.

The wingers wage demands have been a stumbling block in negotiations with potential suitors previously, but after a few months out of the game the Reds may be able to tempt the 26-year-old to Anfield on a more appropriate salary.

Sancho would offer some much-needed depth to Iraola's squad, and Anfield could be the perfect place for the Englishman to revive his career.

articles.title: Texas co-DC Johnny Nansen charged with misdemeanor DWI
articles.summary: Nansen’s availability for Saturday’s matchup against UTSA is now uncertain.
articles.body:
Turmoil continues to surround the Texas Longhorns in the wake of Saturday's comeback victory over the Ohio State Buckeyes in Austin as head coach Steve Sarkisian revealed during a Thursday media availability that co-defensive coordinator/linebackers coach Johnny Nansen was arrested and charged with misdemeanor DWI.

"We obviously are aware of the of the situation. I'm still gathering facts. I'm still monitoring the situation. We're obviously disappointed, but that's all I really have on that at this time," Sarkisian said.

Nansen was not with the team when it practiced on Thursday morning, according to Sarkisian, who was not immediately sure whether the third-year assistant will be on the sidelines with the team when it takes on UTSA at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday at 7 p.m. Central on SEC Network+.

According to a report from Eric Henry of Horns247 , analyst Garrett Cox, who joined new defensive coordinator Will Muschamp from Georgia, was working with the linebackers during Thursday's practice. New NCAA rules allow an unlimited number of on-field coaches during practices and games.

A coaching veteran of nearly 30 years, Nansen has served in a variety of roles under Sarkisian, including as an assistant head coach, running backs coach, and special teams coordinator at Washington from 2009 to 2013 and as a running backs coach and special teams coordinator for two seasons at USC when Sarkisian returned to Los Angeles to lead the Trojans program.

Nansen joined the Texas staff after the 2023 season when Jeff Choate took over as the head coach at Nevada.

Texas has also dealt with controversy surrounding Sarkisian's abbreviated post-game interview with ESPN reporter Holly Rowe and subsequent insensitive comments made by quarterback Arch Manning about an AI video depicting Sarkisian slapping Rowe that required an apology from Manning on Tuesday and from Sarkisian on Thursday.

Now the Longhorns will have to respond to the adversity on Saturday.

"I try to keep the main thing the main thing and focus on what we need to do and that doesn't mean there's not lessons learned along the way and I do think that's important to learn from one another," Sarkisian said.

"But at the same token, this football team has worked really hard for the last eight and a half months to get themselves into this position, and so staying focused on what we need to do when we're in the building, from game prep to meetings to walkthroughs to practice to individual periods to post-practice work. I think that's where our focus is."

articles.title: Wisconsin reveals full conference schedule for upcoming season
articles.summary: The Badgers have their Big Ten schedule for 2027.
articles.body:
Basketball season is less than two months away, and the Big Ten revealed its full conference schedule for the 2026-27 season. The Wisconsin Badgers are set to play 20 games, which means they'll double up against three opponents.

Wisconsin's Big Ten opener will come against the Northwestern Wildcats on December 1st on the road, with their second game. Then, after their annual Marquette game, they return home to face the Purdue Boilermakers on December 8th.

Those are the only two conference games before January, when the rest of the 20-game slate unravels.

Wisconsin will play Iowa, Minnesota, and Illinois twice this year. They've got a couple of notable stretches on the schedule, with the late-season slugfest standing out. The Badgers end the season facing Indiana, Iowa, Illinois, Nebraska, and Michigan State in back-to-back games rotating between home and away.

Wisconsin also won't have any extended home or road trips; they don't have a single three-game stretch across the schedule. Their East Coast travel is also consolidated, as they get five and six-day lays following trips to Maryland and Rutgers.

The Badgers do have some fun road trips. They'll take on Michigan State, UCLA, and Illinois on the road, while Nebraska, Michigan, Purdue, and Illinois all come to the Kohl Center.

This should be a pretty fun and testing schedule for the Badgers alongside a quality non-conference group of opponents.

articles.title: Northwestern extends David Braun’s contract through the 2031 season
articles.summary: David Braun is in his fourth season at Northwestern and currently carries a 20-19 record.
articles.body:
EVANSTON, Ill. — Northwestern has extended coach David Braun's contract through the 2031 season.

The school announced the extension. Financial terms weren't released.

Braun is in his fourth season at Northwestern and carries a 20-19 record into the game with Colorado. Northwestern went 7-6 and beat Central Michigan in the GameAbove Sports Bowl last season.

Northwestern vice president for athletics and recreation Mark Jackson said in a statement that Braun "is everything that we need in a head coach."

"He recruits young men of high character who embrace our elite academic environment and who compete in the most competitive conference in the country," Jackson said. "David develops our student-athletes at a time when retaining talent has never been harder, and they choose to remain Wildcats when other options appear. He does it with a rare combination of relentless competitiveness and integrity."

Braun arrived at Northwestern as a defensive coordinator on Pat Fitzgerald's staff in January 2023 and was named interim head coach later that year after Fitzgerald was fired amid a team hazing scandal. Fitzgerald later sued the school before reaching a settlement.

Northwestern went 8-5 under Braun in 2023 after going 1-11 a year earlier, a turnaround that helped him get the interim tag removed from his title. After slipping to 4-8 in 2024, Northwestern rebounded to earn bowl eligibility last season.

The Wildcats opened the 2026 season by beating South Dakota State 34-18.

"I am so honored to have the opportunity to lead a storied football program at an institution that demands and expects excellence, instills character, and provides a transformative experience for its student-athletes on and off the field," Braun said in a statement released by the school.

Before coming to Northwestern, Braun was a defensive coordinator at the Championship Subdivision level with North Dakota State, which won two titles during his tenure.

Braun was born in Lake Forest, Illinois, about 20 miles from Northwestern's campus.

articles.title: Texas Longhorns linebackers coach Johnny Nansen arrested, charged with misdemeanor DWI
articles.summary: Johnny Nansen, who has been an assistant under Steve Sarkisian at three different schools, was arrested Wednesday night.
articles.body:
AUSTIN - Texas linebackers coach Johnny Nansen was arrested Wednesday night and charged with misdemeanor driving while intoxicated, head coach Steve Sarkisian announced Thursday.

Sarkisian said he doesn't know if Nansen, 52, will be available for the Longhorns' game Saturday against UTSA .

"We had an unfortunate situation last night. We are obviously aware of the situation. I'm still gathering facts," Sarkisian said in his regular weekly online press conference. "I'm still monitoring the situation. We're obviously disappointed, but that's all I really have at this time."

Nansen, who has coached at Texas since 2024 and also serves as co-defensive coordinator, was not at the Longhorns' practice Thursday morning.

Nansen is in his 28th year as a college assistant, first linking up with Sarkisian as his special teams and defensive line coach at Washington in 2009. He followed the head coach when Sarkisian got the head coaching job at USC in 2014. Nansen went on to coach at UCLA and Arizona before rejoining Sarkisian in Austin.

articles.title: Bay Area/Lake Tahoe team makes Eileen Gu top pick in X Games Winter League draft
articles.summary: Eileen Gu, the freestyle skier and six-time Olympic medalist from San Francisco, was the No. 1 overall choice Wednesday ahead of the X Games Winter League's...
articles.body:
Eileen Gu, the freestyle skier and six-time Olympic medalist from San Francisco, was the No. 1 overall choice in Wednesday night's draft ahead of the inaugural season for the X Games Winter League.

XC Golden State, the franchise representing the Bay Area and Lake Tahoe, chose Gu with the first pick of the draft, held in Los Angeles.

Gu, one of the winter league's "athlete founders," shared her reaction to the news in a video posted on Instagram.

"I just wanted to say how honored and grateful I am to be the first overall draft pick," she said. "I'm really excited to make something super magical happen this season. … I think this league is going to be so big for our industry and our sport."

Gu, 23, stirred international controversy in 2019, when she announced she would compete for China, her mother's birth country. Gu was raised in San Francisco: She attended University High School and competed for the U.S. in her youth.

She won two gold medals and one silver in freestyle skiing at the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing. Then, at the Winter Games in Italy earlier this year, Gu earned another gold medal and two more silvers.

Wednesday night's draft featured each of the four teams – Golden State, New York, Park City and Whistler – selecting 10 athletes from skiing and snowboarding. Golden State's second pick was Luca Harrington, a skier from New Zealand, and its other choices included one skier (Lainey Steen) and one snowboarder (Lily Dhawornavej) from Colorado.

In addition to Gu, the other first-round draft choices were Canadian snowboarder Mark McMorris (New York), Chinese snowboarder Yiming Su (Park City) and Canadian skier Megan Oldham (Whistler).

The X Games Winter League announced this week that its maiden season would feature three events – in Aspen (Jan. 29-31), Calgary (Feb. 19-21) and Ruka, Finland (April 9-11).
